hoursWeeklyScheduleThis field gives the hours of each week, in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), when the station uses this frequency. When the record does not have this field, the station uses the frequency during the hours of the operating location.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about this frequency, as free text.
roleenumyesThis field gives the role of the station on this frequency, as one of the enumerated values.
  • tower This value identifies the aerodrome control tower. On a carrier, it is the primary flight control.
  • ground This value identifies the ground control for the movement area.
  • clearance_delivery This value identifies the clearance delivery for instrument flight rules (IFR) clearances before taxi.
  • approach This value identifies the approach control. On a military airfield, it is the radar approach control (RAPCON).
  • departure This value identifies the departure control. It controls instrument flight rules (IFR) flights after they take off, until the en-route centre controls them.
  • atis This value identifies the automatic terminal information service (ATIS) broadcast, which gives the weather, the active runway and other airfield information all the time.
  • ops This value identifies the operations desk of the unit or of the forward arming and refuelling point (FARP).
  • pmsv This value identifies the pilot-to-metro service (PMSV) for weather information.
  • unicom This value identifies the universal communications (UNICOM) at an airfield without a control tower.
  • marshal This value identifies the carrier marshal control for recovery.
  • final This value identifies the final controller of a precision approach radar (PAR) approach. The final controller gives the azimuth and glide path corrections.

TaxiEdge

A taxi edge is a taxi route between two taxi nodes.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
categoryenumThis field gives the largest aircraft class that can use the edge, as one of the enumerated values.
  • fighter This value identifies fighters and other small aircraft.
  • medium This value identifies aircraft of moderate dimensions, for example a transport aircraft with two engines.
  • heavy This value identifies heavy aircraft, for example a tanker aircraft or a large transport aircraft.
  • helicopter This value identifies a stand or a taxiway only for helicopters, not for fixed-wing aircraft.
fromIdentifieryesThis field identifies the taxi node that is at the start of the edge. The value shall be the identifier of a node of this graph.
one_waybooleanThe value is true when aircraft can taxi on the edge only from from to to. The value is false when aircraft can taxi on the edge in the two directions.
taxiwaystringThis field gives the name of the taxiway of the edge, for example Alpha, as free text.
toIdentifieryesThis field identifies the taxi node that is at the end of the edge. The value shall be the identifier of a different node of this graph.
widthLengthThis field gives the width of the taxiway of the edge, as a length with its unit.

TaxiGraph

A taxi graph is the taxi routes of an airfield as nodes and edges. A program finds a taxi route along the edges from a parking stand to a hold-short node.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
edgeslist of TaxiEdgeyesThis list contains the edges between the taxi nodes.
nodeslist of TaxiNodeyesThis list contains the taxi nodes of the airfield.

TaxiNode

A taxi node is one point of the taxi graph.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this taxi node. Each taxi node in its airfield has a different identifier.
kindenumThis field gives the type of the taxi node, as one of the enumerated values. A hold_short or runway_connection node shall have runway_end. A parking node shall have stand.
  • hold_short This value identifies a hold-short point before a runway. Aircraft stop at this point until they get a clearance.
  • runway_connection This value identifies a point where a taxiway connects to a runway. Aircraft go onto the runway or off the runway at this point.
  • runway This value identifies a point on the runway centreline.
  • intersection This value identifies a point where two or more taxiways connect.
  • parking This value identifies a point where the taxi graph connects to a parking stand.
namestringThis field gives the name of the taxi node, for example A3, as free text.
positionGeoPointyesThis field gives the geographic position of the taxi node, as latitude and longitude.
runway_endRunwayDesignatorThis field gives the designator of the runway end to which this node connects, or before which aircraft stop at this node. The value shall be the designator of an end of a runway of this airfield.
standIdentifierThis field identifies the parking stand that this node connects to. The value shall be the identifier of a stand of this airfield.

TrafficPattern

A traffic pattern is a set of pattern values, with more values for each aircraft category. A consumer gets each value from the runway end first, then from the airfield, and then from the traffic pattern profile. A value for an aircraft category replaces the general value for that aircraft category.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
altitudeAltitude & anyThis field gives the altitude of the rectangular traffic pattern, as an altitude with its unit and reference. The reference is above ground level or mean sea level.
break_pointenumThis field gives the position along the runway at which aircraft start the overhead break, as one of the enumerated values.
  • approach_end The overhead break starts above the approach end of the runway.
  • midfield The overhead break starts above the middle of the runway.
  • departure_end The overhead break starts above the departure end of the runway.
categoriesobjectThis field gives the pattern values for each aircraft category. Each aircraft category gives only the values that are different.
departure_ceilingAltitude & anyThis field gives the highest altitude for departures while aircraft use the overhead pattern, as an altitude with its unit and reference. The reference is above ground level or mean sea level.
directionenumThis field gives the direction of the turns in the traffic pattern, as one of the enumerated values.
  • left Each turn in the pattern is a left turn.
  • right Each turn in the pattern is a right turn.
go_aroundGoAroundThis field gives the go-around instructions of the pattern.
initiallist of InitialPointThis list contains the initial points of the overhead pattern.
overhead_altitudeAltitude & anyThis field gives the altitude of the initial leg and of the overhead break, as an altitude with its unit and reference. The reference is above ground level or mean sea level.
profileIdentifierThis field identifies the traffic pattern profile that gives the values that this pattern does not give.
reentryReentryThis field gives the re-entry procedure of the overhead pattern.
sfoSimulatedFlameoutThis field gives the simulated flameout (SFO) pattern. When the record has no SFO pattern, the pattern values do not give one.

Airspace

urn:openaix:schema:airspace:0.2.0-draft.1

airspace

Airspace is a region of airspace with a name, made of volumes that each have a horizontal boundary and vertical limits. The airspace_type field gives the class or the type of operation. Shelves, sectors and subtracted volumes use the same structure of components. The control measures for air traffic in Annex B use this contract. Examples are class B airspace, control zones and restricted areas.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
activeActivationyesThis field gives the time interval during which this airspace is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.
airspace_class_codeenumThis field gives the airspace class that the source gives, as one of the enumerated values. When the code is empty, the source gives no class. All classes use the same structure for geometry and altitude.
  • A
  • B
  • C
  • D
  • E
  • F
  • G
airspace_typeenumyesThis field gives the class or type of operation of the airspace, such as ClassB, ClassD, MTA or TMA, as one of the enumerated values. MTA is a military training area, and TMA is a terminal control area.
  • ClassA International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class A airspace is airspace only for instrument flight rules (IFR) flights. All flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary. ATC separates all flights from each other.
  • ClassB International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class B airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. All flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary. ATC separates all flights from each other. In the United States, ATC separates VFR flights with radar. When the radar does not operate, ATC stops this service for VFR flights.
  • ClassC International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class C airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. All flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary. ATC separates IFR flights from all other flights, and VFR flights from IFR flights. VFR flights get traffic information about other VFR flights. In the United States, a VFR flight gets radio contact with ATC before it goes in. An ATC clearance is not necessary.
  • ClassD International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class D airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. All flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary. ATC separates IFR flights only from other IFR flights. IFR flights get traffic information about VFR flights, and VFR flights get traffic information about all other flights. In the United States, a VFR flight gets radio contact with ATC before it goes in. An ATC clearance is not necessary.
  • ClassE International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class E airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. Only IFR flights get air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is necessary only for IFR flights. ATC separates IFR flights only from other IFR flights. All flights get traffic information as far as practical. A control zone cannot be class E airspace.
  • ClassF International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class F airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. No flight gets air traffic control (ATC) service, and an ATC clearance is not necessary. Participating IFR flights get an air traffic advisory service, which separates them from other IFR flights as far as practical. All flights get flight information service when they ask for it. The United States does not use class F airspace.
  • ClassG International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class G airspace is airspace for instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR) flights. No flight gets air traffic control (ATC) service or separation, and an ATC clearance is not necessary. All flights get flight information service when they ask for it.
  • MTA A military training area (MTA) is a geographical area that is temporarily or permanently for education and training, which includes exercises and testing. It can include airspace. AJP-3.3.5 gives this area as the training area (TRNG).
  • MOA A military operations area (MOA) is airspace that is not in class A airspace. It separates flight training of armed forces that is not dangerous from instrument flight rules (IFR) aircraft. It also shows visual flight rules (VFR) aircraft where this training occurs. When it is active, air traffic control (ATC) lets an IFR flight go through it only when ATC can separate the flight.
  • CTA A control area (CTA) is controlled airspace that extends upwards from a given limit above the surface. Its floor is above the surface, not at the surface. Air traffic control (ATC) gives ATC service to instrument flight rules (IFR) flights in it. Its International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class sets the ATC service for visual flight rules (VFR) flights.
  • CTR A control zone (CTR) is controlled airspace from the surface to a given upper limit. Air traffic control (ATC) gives ATC service to instrument flight rules (IFR) flights in it. Its International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class sets the ATC service for visual flight rules (VFR) flights.
  • TMA A terminal control area (TMA) is a control area, usually at the confluence of air traffic services routes near one or more major aerodromes. Air traffic control (ATC) gives ATC service to instrument flight rules (IFR) flights in it. Its International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) class sets the ATC service for visual flight rules (VFR) flights.
  • FIR A flight information region (FIR) is airspace of defined dimensions in which flight information service and alerting service are available.
  • UIR An upper flight information region (UIR) is a flight information region (FIR) above a different FIR. Its floor is the ceiling of the lower FIR and is a visual flight rules (VFR) cruising level. Its procedures can be different from the procedures of the lower FIR.
  • ATZ An aerodrome traffic zone (ATZ) is airspace of defined dimensions around an aerodrome. Its function is the protection of aerodrome traffic.
  • ADIZ An air defence identification zone (ADIZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in which the identification, location and control of aircraft is immediately necessary.
  • TRA A temporary reserved area (TRA) is a defined volume of airspace that one airspace authority usually controls. By common agreement, it is temporarily for another airspace authority. Other air traffic may transit it only with air traffic control (ATC) clearance.
  • TSA A temporary segregated area (TSA) is airspace of defined dimensions for the exclusive use of specified users. Their tasks make this necessary. It is for a set period, and no other traffic uses the airspace.
  • ROZ A restricted operating zone (ROZ) is airspace of defined dimensions that the airspace control authority designates for a given situation or operational need. Examples are refuelling orbits, holding, fires and landing or drop zones. It restricts the operation of one or more airspace users in it.
  • Restricted A restricted area is airspace of defined dimensions above the land areas or territorial waters of a state. In it, the conditions that the state gives restrict the flight of aircraft.
  • Prohibited A prohibited area is airspace of defined dimensions above the land areas or territorial waters of a state. The state prohibits flight in it.
  • Danger A danger area is airspace of defined dimensions in which tasks that are dangerous to the flight of aircraft can occur at stated times. This definition comes from air traffic control.
  • Warning A warning area is airspace of known dimensions that starts 3 nautical miles from the coast of the United States. It contains tasks that can be dangerous to non-participating aircraft. Its function is to tell the pilots of non-participating aircraft about this risk. It can be above the waters of the United States, above international waters or above the two.
  • Alert An alert area is airspace that can contain a large quantity of pilot training or an unusual type of flight. This training and these flights are not dangerous to aircraft. Charts show the area to tell the pilots of non-participating aircraft about it. All flights in it obey the Code of Federal Regulations. Each pilot in it has the same task of collision avoidance.
  • Sector A control sector is airspace of known horizontal and vertical dimensions. One controller or a group of controllers controls the air traffic in it. The primary traffic flows, the altitude layers and the work of the controllers set its limits. Pilots in it usually speak to air traffic control (ATC) on the frequencies of the sector.
  • ATCAA An air traffic control assigned airspace (ATCAA) is airspace of defined vertical and lateral limits that air traffic control (ATC) assigns. It separates the stated activities in it from other instrument flight rules (IFR) air traffic.
  • CFA A controlled firing area (CFA) is airspace that contains activities that are a danger to non-participating aircraft when they are not in a controlled environment. They stop at once when spotter aircraft, radar or ground observers find an aircraft that approaches.
  • NSA A national security area (NSA) is airspace of defined vertical and lateral dimensions at locations with ground facilities. At these locations, it is necessary to increase security and safety. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) tells pilots to avoid flight through it. A temporary flight restriction (TFR) can temporarily close it to flight.
  • TFR A temporary flight restriction (TFR) is a regulatory action of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) in a notice to air missions (NOTAM). It temporarily restricts some aircraft from operation in a defined area. Its function is the protection of persons or property in the air or on the ground.
  • SFRA A special flight rules area (SFRA) is airspace of defined dimensions, above land areas or territorial waters. In it, the flight of aircraft obeys 14 CFR part 93, unless air traffic control (ATC) authorizes otherwise.
  • TRSA A terminal radar service area (TRSA) is airspace around a designated airport. In it, air traffic control (ATC) gives radar vectoring, sequencing and separation full time. This service is for all instrument flight rules (IFR) aircraft and participating visual flight rules (VFR) aircraft. This service is not mandatory for pilots. It is not an airspace class.
  • ModeCVeil A mode C veil is the airspace that is 30 nautical miles or less from an airport in Appendix D, section 1 of 14 CFR part 91. It goes from the surface to 10,000 feet above mean sea level (MSL). Unless air traffic control (ATC) authorizes a different procedure, aircraft in it have a serviceable transponder with automatic altitude reporting and serviceable ADS-B Out equipment.
  • RMZ A radio mandatory zone (RMZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in which the carriage and operation of radio equipment is mandatory.
  • TMZ A transponder mandatory zone (TMZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in which the carriage and operation of a pressure-altitude reporting transponder is mandatory.
  • Other The airspace has a local type that is not in this list. The local_type field gives the local name of the type.
channelslist of IdentifierThis list identifies the communications channels of this airspace.
componentslist of AirspaceComponentyesThis list contains the airspace volumes of this airspace, in order. Each volume has a floor and a ceiling.
controlling_agencyIdentifierThis field identifies the agency that controls the operations in this airspace.
coordination_instructionslist of stringThis list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this airspace has an effect on.
descriptionstringThis field gives the information about this airspace and its local conditions, as free text.
designatorstringThis field gives the designator that a publication or an assignment gives to the airspace. An example is the designator of a restricted area.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this airspace. Other records and orders use it to refer to this airspace.
local_typestringThis field gives the local type name of the airspace when airspace_type is Other, as free text.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this airspace, for display.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about this airspace, as free text.
purposestringThis field gives the task or objective of this airspace, as free text.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this airspace. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
restrictionslist of stringThis list contains the conditions that control the operations in this airspace.
statestringThis field gives the State responsible for the airspace, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code such as DEU. Under International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Annex 11, paragraph 2.1, this State is responsible for the air traffic services in the airspace. An example is the State of a flight information region (FIR).
type"AIRSPACE"yesThe value identifies this record as an airspace, which is a region made of airspace volumes.

Airway

urn:openaix:schema:airway:0.2.0-draft.1

airway

An airway is an en-route route as a sequence of fixes, with the course, the distance and the altitude limits of each segment.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
airway_typeenumyesThis field gives the class of the airway, as one of the enumerated values.
  • advisory This value identifies a designated route along which air traffic advisory service is available.
  • airway This value identifies a control area, or a part of it, in the shape of a corridor. Radio navigation aids identify the corridor.
  • area_navigation This value identifies an air traffic services (ATS) route for aircraft that can do area navigation.
  • air_traffic_services This value identifies a specified route that channels the flow of traffic, as necessary to supply air traffic services.
  • conditional This value identifies an air traffic services (ATS) route, or a part of it, that is non-permanent. Aircraft plan and use it only under stated conditions.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this airway. Other resources and orders use this stable identifier to refer to this airway.
identstringThis field identifies this airway as published. An example is V356.
levelenumThis field gives the altitude structure of the airway, as one of the enumerated values.
  • low This value identifies the low altitude structure.
  • high This value identifies the high altitude structure.
  • both This value identifies the low and the high altitude structures.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this airway, for display.
provenanceProvenanceThis field gives the provenance of this airway as structured data: how the data were made, the authority, the aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle and the tool that made them.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this airway. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
segmentslist of objectyesThis list contains the fixes, in airway sequence, in order. Each item has a fix and the segment from that fix to the next fix.
sourcestringThis field gives the source of this record. The value gives the authority that publishes the data, and the cycle, for example FAA CIFP cycle 2610. A record that an author writes does not have this field. The field provenance gives the same facts as structured data.
type"AIRWAY"yesThe value identifies this record as a control measure for an airway, with the catalogue code AIRWAY. The value selects this contract in a catalogue of control measures.

Command and control agency

urn:openaix:schema:c2-agency:0.2.0-draft.1

c2-agency

A command and control agency is an organization with a call sign and a role in operations. Units contact it on its radio channels.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastring (uri)This field identifies the schema that validates this document.
areaslist of Geometry_polygon | AgencyArea | ControlMeasureSelection | Geometry_rectangle | Geometry_ellipse | Geometry_geojson_polygonThis list contains the areas that the agency covers. Each item is a polygon (an openAIX polygon or a GeoJSON polygon), a planning area or a control measure.
callsignstringyesThis field gives the radio call sign of the agency, as free text.
channelslist of IdentifierThis list identifies the radio channels that other units use to contact the agency.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this agency. Other records and orders use it to refer to this agency.
kind"c2-agency"yesThe value identifies this record as a command and control agency.
platformenumThis field gives the platform of the agency: on the ground (ground) or in an aircraft (airborne), as one of the enumerated values.
  • ground
  • airborne
positionGeoPointThis field gives the geographic position of the agency, as latitude and longitude. The field is applicable only to an agency that does not move.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the external resource catalogue that resolves the references of this record. The reference identifies the catalogue and gives its revision.
roleenumyesThis field gives the command and control function of the agency, as one of the enumerated values.
  • AOC This value identifies the air operations centre (AOC), which plans, controls and assesses air operations. It publishes the air tasking order (ATO) and the airspace control order (ACO).
  • CRC This value identifies the control and reporting centre (CRC), which is an element on the ground for surveillance, identification and control of air operations.
  • ASOC This value identifies the air support operations centre (ASOC), which controls the air operations that help ground forces directly.
  • DASC This value identifies the direct air support centre (DASC), which is the Marine Corps agency that controls the air operations that help ground forces directly.
  • TACP This value identifies a tactical air control party (TACP), which is an air liaison element with a ground unit. It sends air support requests and gives terminal attack control.
  • AWACS This value identifies the Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS), which gives airborne surveillance, early warning and control.
  • JTAC This value identifies a joint terminal attack controller (JTAC), who controls close air support (CAS) aircraft from a forward position.
  • ATC This value identifies air traffic control (ATC), which gives air traffic services such as approach control, tower control or range control.

AgencyArea

An area selection is a reference to one planning area of the resource catalogue.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
areaIdentifieryesThis field identifies the planning area that the agency covers.

openAIX common resources

urn:openaix:schema:common:0.2.0-draft.1

common

Definitions for all openAIX documents are the identifiers, positions, geometry, units, time intervals and resource references that more than one type of document contains.

Type: any

Activation

An activation is the time when a control measure is available. It is an interval, a Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) schedule for each week in an interval, or continuous activation.

Type: Window | ScheduledWindow | object

AirspaceComponent

An airspace component is one part of an airspace in three dimensions, with a boundary, a floor and a ceiling. Each component adds a volume, subtracts a volume or intersects a volume, in sequence.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
activeActivationThis field gives the time interval during which this component is available, in the time interval of the parent control measure. This field is optional.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
geometryGeometry_polygon | Geometry_circle | Geometry_sector | Geometry_polyarc | Geometry_corridor | Geometry_rectangle | Geometry_ellipse | Geometry_geojson_polygonyesThis field gives the horizontal boundary of this component: points, distances and bearings in a format for a simulator. A geojson geometry (RFC 7946) of the same shape is also correct.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this component. Each component in its parent airspace has a different identifier.
lower_limitVerticalLimityesThis field gives the floor of this component: an altitude with its reference, or the surface.
maximum_limitAltitudeThis field gives the maximum limit of this component, as an altitude with its unit and reference. Where this value is higher than upper_limit, it increases the ceiling. Each value keeps its reference.
minimum_limitAltitudeThis field gives the minimum floor of this component, as an altitude with its unit and reference. Where this value is higher than lower_limit, it replaces the floor. To compare limits with different references, a consumer uses terrain or atmospheric data.
namestringThis field gives the name of this sector or shelf, for display.
operationenumyesThis field gives the operation of this component on the volume that the components before it make, as one of the enumerated values. The components operate in the sequence of the array, and the first component adds a volume.
  • add
  • subtract
  • intersect
upper_limitVerticalLimityesThis field gives the ceiling of this component: an altitude with its reference, or no limit.

Altitude

An altitude is a vertical position with its unit and its reference: mean sea level (MSL), above ground level (AGL) or flight level (FL).

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
referenceenumyesThis field gives the vertical reference of the altitude, as one of the enumerated values. The value is mean sea level (MSL), above ground level (AGL) or flight level (FL).
  • MSL
  • AGL
  • FL
unitenumyesThis field gives the unit of the altitude: feet, metres or flight level, as one of the enumerated values.
  • ft
  • m
  • flight_level
valuenumberyesThis field gives the value of the altitude, in the unit of unit.

AltitudeBlock

An altitude block is a vertical band between a floor and a ceiling. The floor can be the surface, and the ceiling can have no limit.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
lowerVerticalLimityesThis field gives the floor of the altitude block: an altitude with its reference, or the surface.
upperVerticalLimityesThis field gives the ceiling of the altitude block: an altitude with its reference, or no limit.

Bearing

A bearing is a direction with its value and its north reference: true north or magnetic north. A magnetic bearing keeps the reference that its author gives. The declination is optional. When the declination is not available, a consumer should show that it cannot change the bearing to true north.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
declination_degnumberThis field gives the magnetic declination that changes a bearing from true north to magnetic north, in degrees. This field is optional.
referenceenumyesThis field gives the north reference of the bearing: true north or magnetic north, as one of the enumerated values.
  • true
  • magnetic
valuenumberyesThis field gives the value of the bearing, in degrees from 0 to less than 360.

BearingRange

A bearing range is a range of bearings from a start bearing clockwise to an end bearing.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
end_bearingBearingyesThis field gives the end of the range of bearings, as a bearing with its unit and reference.
start_bearingBearingyesThis field gives the start of the range of bearings, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

CasBrief

A close air support (CAS) brief is the data that the aircrew get for one CAS attack: the 9-line data of JP 3-09.3 and the mission-level data of the air tasking order (ATO). The ATO and the operation order (OPORD) use this one definition. A field that a use does not need stays out of the record. JP 3-09.3 (2014) Chapter V gives the check-in briefing and the CAS brief.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
ato_missionIdentifierThis field identifies the mission of the air tasking order (ATO) that receives the brief. The orders field of the operation order (OPORD) identifies the ATO.
check_inCheckInThis field gives the check-in data for the controller.
contact_pointslist of ControlMeasureSelectionThis list identifies the contact points that the aircraft fly to before the controller gives them a task. Each point shall have the role control.
control_typeenumThis field gives the type of terminal attack control, as one of the enumerated values.
  • type_1 This value identifies type 1 terminal attack control, in which the controller sees the target and the aircraft.
  • type_2 This value identifies type 2 terminal attack control, in which the controller does not see the target or the aircraft.
  • type_3 This value identifies type 3 terminal attack control, in which the controller gives clearance for all attacks in an area.
controllerIdentifierThis field identifies the command and control agency that gives the brief.
controllerslist of ControllerContactThis list contains the agencies and radio channels that control the close air support (CAS) for this brief.
danger_closebooleanThe value is true when the friendly forces are inside the danger-close distance of the weapons for the attack. The value is false when the friendly forces are outside that distance.
distanceLengthThis field gives the distance from the initial point to the target, as a length with its unit.
egress_pointIdentifierThis field identifies the point that is the egress point. The point shall have the role egress.
final_attack_headingslist of BearingRangeThis list contains the ranges of final attack headings that the aircraft can use for the attack. Each range goes clockwise from its start bearing to its end bearing.
fire_support_measureslist of ControlMeasureSelectionThis list identifies the fire support coordination measures that apply to the close air support (CAS) mission.
friendly_directionenumThis field gives the direction from the target to the nearest friendly forces, as one of the enumerated values.
  • north
  • north_east
  • east
  • south_east
  • south
  • south_west
  • west
  • north_west
friendly_distanceLengthThis field gives the distance from the target to the nearest friendly forces, as a length with its unit.
friendly_lineslist of ControlMeasureSelectionThis list identifies the lines and boundaries that show the positions of the friendly ground forces.
friendly_markingFriendlyMarkingThis field gives the means that marks the position of the nearest friendly forces, as one of the enumerated values.
ground_scheme_summarystringThis field gives the plan of the friendly ground forces, in short form, as free text.
hazardslist of HazardThis list contains the hazards in the target area that are not threats.
headingBearingThis field gives the heading from the initial point to the target, as a bearing with its unit and reference.
holdinglist of ControlMeasureSelectionThis list identifies the orbits, points or zones that the aircraft use to hold before they get a task.
holding_altitudeAltitudeBlockThis field gives the vertical limits of the holding stack, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling.
idIdentifierThis field identifies this close air support (CAS) brief. Each CAS brief in the order has a different identifier. Other parts of the order use it to refer to this CAS brief.
initial_pointIdentifierThis field identifies the point that is the initial point of the attack. The point shall have the role initial.
initial_pointslist of ControlMeasureSelectionThis list identifies the initial points that start the attack runs of the aircraft. Each point shall have the role initial.
laser_codeLaserCodeThis field gives the code of the laser mark, as a laser code with its unit.
laser_codeslist of LaserCodeThis list contains the laser codes for the controller and the aircraft in this brief.
laser_target_lineBearingThis field gives the laser target line, as a bearing with its unit and reference.
markTargetMarkThis field gives the type of mark of the target, as one of the enumerated values.
markslist of TargetMarkThis list contains the types of target mark that the controller can supply. JP 3-09.3 (2014) gives these marks.
method_of_attackenumThis field gives the method of attack, as one of the enumerated values.
  • bomb_on_target
  • bomb_on_coordinate
offset_directionenumThis field gives the side of the line from the initial point to the target on which the aircraft fly the attack, as one of the enumerated values.
  • left The aircraft fly the attack to the left of the line from the initial point to the target.
  • right The aircraft fly the attack to the right of the line from the initial point to the target.
remarksstringThis field gives the notes for the aircrews that are not in the other fields of this brief, as free text.
targetIdentifierThis field identifies the target of the resource catalogue that the brief is for.
target_descriptionstringThis field gives the target description, as free text.
target_elevationElevationThis field gives the elevation of the target, as an elevation with its unit.
target_positionGeoPointThis field gives the geographic position of the target, as latitude and longitude.
threatslist of IdentifierThis list identifies the threats of the resource catalogue that are a danger to the aircraft in the target area.
time_on_targetDateTimeThis field gives the time at which the weapons hit the target.
time_to_target_secondsnumberThis field gives the time from the time of the brief to the time on target, in seconds.

CheckIn

A close air support (CAS) check-in is the data that the CAS aircrew gives to the controller at check-in. JP 3-09.3 (2014) Figure V-4 gives the check-in briefing.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
abort_codestringThis field gives the abort code for the controller and the aircrew, as free text.
itemslist of enumThis list contains the parts of the check-in briefing that the aircrew gives.
  • mission_number
  • aircraft_number_and_type
  • position_and_altitude
  • ordnance
  • time_on_station
  • capabilities
  • abort_code
procedureIdentifierThis field identifies the procedure that gives the check-in steps.

ClassificationLevel

A classification level is a security classification of the American government that the banner of an operation order (OPORD) can show.

Type: enum

  • UNCLASSIFIED
  • CUI
  • CONFIDENTIAL
  • SECRET
  • TOP SECRET

Coalition

A coalition is the side of a record in the simulation: blue, red or neutral. It is simulator data, not real-world data.

Type: enum

  • blue
  • red
  • neutral

ControlMeasure

A control measure is one openAIX control measure: a reference to one control measure contract, or an extension control measure with a namespace. The type field selects the contract.

Type: measure-aca | airspace | airway | measure-aor | measure-area | measure-cl | measure-fire-support-line | measure-isr | measure-kb | measure-line | measure-mez | measure-misarc | navaid | orbit | point | measure-route | territory | measure-tl | measure-volume | object

ControlMeasureSelection

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies the control measure of this selection.
kind"control_measure"yesThe value identifies this record as a control measure selection. The value is control_measure.

ControllerContact

An agency channel is an agency for the aircrew, with its radio channels.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
agencyIdentifieryesThis field identifies the agency or forward air controller that the aircrew speaks to. The value is the identifier of a command and control agency or of a forward air controller (FAC) of the resource catalogue.
alternate_channelIdentifierThis field identifies the alternative radio channel that connects the aircrew and the agency when the primary channel is not available.
channelIdentifierThis field identifies the primary radio channel that connects the aircrew and the agency.

DCSData

Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) data is the data of a record for DCS. The bindings field contains the objects in a DCS mission that are this record or that show it. The other fields contain DCS values that are not objects of a mission.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
alic_codeintegerThis field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) aircraft launcher interface computer (ALIC) code of the radar. The high-speed anti-radiation missile (HARM) of the DCS F-16C uses this code. Appendix B of the DCS F-16C Early Access Guide gives the codes.
angle_degnumberThis field gives the drawing angle from the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) mission, in degrees. This angle is not a true bearing or a magnetic bearing. Only a consumer with a correct adapter for DCS should use this angle to turn the shape.
beaconobjectThis field gives the radio beacon of the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) object that the record is bound to: the identification, the frequency and the channel as the DCS database gives them. They can differ from the published values of the real station, which the core fields of the record give. The record has at least one of them.
bindingslist of DCSObjectRefThis list contains the objects in a Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) mission that are this record or show it on the map. The record keeps its geometry in latitude and longitude, independently of these objects.
clsidstringThis field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) class identifier (CLSID) of the load on the pylon. For a rack, the CLSID identifies the rack together with its stores.
clsidslist of stringThis list contains the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) class identifiers (CLSID) that agree with this store.
coalitionCoalitionThis field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) coalition of the record: blue, red or neutral, as one of the enumerated values. The coalition is the side of the record in the DCS mission.
labelstringThis field gives the label of the pylon in the mission editor.
objectslist of DCSObjectRefThis list contains the units, groups or static objects in a Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) mission that are parts of the aimpoint.
payloadobjectThis field identifies the load in the UnitPayloads file of the aircraft that agrees with this standard conventional load (SCL).
projectionstringThis field identifies the theatre projection of Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) that gives the dimensions and the drawing angle.
pylonintegerThis field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) pylon number of this station.
settingsobjectThis field contains the values of the pylon in the mission editor, such as the fuze values. The record keeps them for round trips.
typestringThis field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) type name of the aircraft type, for example F-16C_50.

DCSObjectRef

A Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) object reference is a link to one object in a DCS mission. The record that contains this reference keeps its geometry in latitude and longitude, independently of this identifier.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
angle_degnumberThis field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) angle of a point or circle drawing, in degrees. The angle is not a true bearing.
closedbooleanThe value is true when the line drawing is a closed shape. The value is false when the line drawing is an open line.
group_categoryenumThis field gives the class of the group: airplane, helicopter, vehicle, ship or train, as one of the enumerated values.
  • airplane
  • helicopter
  • vehicle
  • ship
  • train
iconstringThis field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) identifier of the icon file.
kindenumyesThis field gives the type of the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) object, as one of the enumerated values. The types are units, groups, static objects, scenery objects, airbases, parking stands, drawings and trigger zones.
  • unit
  • group
  • static
  • scenery
  • airbase
  • stand
  • drawing
  • trigger_zone
layerstringThis field gives the drawing layer in the mission editor, such as Blue or Author.
line_modeenumThis field gives the mode of a line drawing in Digital Combat Simulator (DCS), as one of the enumerated values.
  • segment
  • segments
  • free
mission_idstringThis field identifies the mission in which a consumer resolves names and number identifiers. This field is optional.
namestringThis field gives the name of this Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) object, for display.
native_fieldsobjectThis field contains the attributes from Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) that have no typed field. The record keeps them for round trips. A typed field for identifiers, geometry or style shall not go in this object.
object_idintegerThis field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) number that identifies the object in the mission.
polygon_modeenumThis field gives the mode of a polygon drawing in Digital Combat Simulator (DCS), as one of the enumerated values.
  • circle
  • oval
  • rect
  • free
  • arrow
primitive_typeenumThis field gives the drawing primitive in Digital Combat Simulator (DCS), as one of the enumerated values. The value is a polygon, a line, a text box or an icon.
  • Polygon
  • Line
  • TextBox
  • Icon
styleobjectThis field contains display attributes from the mission editor, when they are known. The geometry does not change with them.
textstringThis field gives the text of a text box drawing, as free text.
unit_typestringThis field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) type name of the unit or the static object, when known.
zone_typeenumThis field gives the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) type of the trigger zone, as one of the enumerated values. The value circle is zone type 0, and the value quad is zone type 2.
  • circle
  • quad

DateTime

A date-time is an RFC 3339 date-time with a Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) designator or an offset from UTC, such as 2026-10-02T06:00:00Z.

Type: string (date-time)

DocumentRef

A document reference is a document that a record refers to. Consumers do not get the document automatically through a network.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
idstringyesThis field identifies the document that the record refers to.
pathstringThis field gives the file path of the document.
revisionstringThis field gives the revision of the document.
sectionstringThis field gives the part of the document that the record refers to, such as a section or a paragraph.
titlestringThis field gives the title of the document.

Elevation

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
reference"MSL"yesThis field gives the vertical reference of the elevation. The value is always MSL.
unitenumyesThis field gives the unit of the elevation: feet or metres, as one of the enumerated values.
  • ft
  • m
valuenumberyesThis field gives the value of the elevation, in the unit of unit.

Extensions

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
simSimDataThis field contains the simulator data of the record, with the simulator identifier as the key.

Frequency

A frequency is a radio frequency in kilohertz or megahertz. The modulation is amplitude modulation (AM) or frequency modulation (FM). The modulation and the radio band are optional.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
bandenumThis field gives the radio band of the frequency, as one of the enumerated values. The band shall agree with the value of the frequency. The limits are 2 to 30 MHz for high frequency (HF), and 30 to 88 MHz for frequency modulation (FM). The limits are 108 to 174 MHz for very high frequency (VHF), and 225 to 400 MHz for ultra high frequency (UHF).
  • hf This value identifies the high frequency (HF) band, from 3 to 30 MHz, for radio communication at long range.
  • fm This value identifies the very high frequency (VHF) band with frequency modulation (FM) that army radios use, from 30 to 88 MHz.
  • vhf This value identifies the very high frequency (VHF) band of aircraft radios, from 118 to 137 MHz.
  • uhf This value identifies the ultra high frequency (UHF) band of the aircraft radios of armed forces, from 225 to 400 MHz.
modulationenumThis field gives the modulation of the radio frequency: amplitude modulation (AM) or frequency modulation (FM), as one of the enumerated values. This field is optional.
  • AM
  • FM
unitenumyesThis field gives the unit of the frequency: kilohertz or megahertz, as one of the enumerated values.
  • kHz
  • MHz
valuenumberyesThis field gives the value of the frequency, in the unit of unit.

FriendlyMarking

A friendly marking is the means that marks the position of the friendly forces for the aircrew.

Type: enum

  • panel This value identifies a panel with a bright colour on the ground.
  • smoke This value identifies coloured smoke from a grenade or a canister at the friendly position.
  • mirror This value identifies a mirror that reflects the light of the sun.
  • strobe This value identifies a visible strobe light that flashes at the friendly position.
  • infrared_strobe This value identifies an infrared strobe light that aircrew with night vision devices can see.
  • chemical_light This value identifies a chemical light stick that gives light for a short time, usually at night.
  • flare This value identifies a pyrotechnic flare that burns bright at the friendly position.

GeoJSONLineString

A GeoJSON line string is a GeoJSON geometry object of the type LineString, as in RFC 7946.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
bboxlist of numberThis list contains the limits of the bounding box of the geometry, as in RFC 7946 section 5.
coordinateslist of GeoJSONPositionyesThis list contains the positions of the line string, in order. Each item is a GeoJSON position.
type"LineString"yesThe value identifies this record as a GeoJSON LineString.

GeoJSONLinearRing

A GeoJSON linear ring is a closed sequence of four or more positions. The first position and the last position shall be the same.

Type: list of GeoJSONPosition

GeoJSONMultiPolygon

A GeoJSON multipolygon is a GeoJSON geometry object of the type MultiPolygon, as in RFC 7946.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
bboxlist of numberThis list contains the limits of the bounding box of the geometry, as in RFC 7946 section 5.
coordinateslist of list of GeoJSONLinearRingyesThis list contains the polygons of the multipolygon. Each polygon is a list of linear rings, as in a GeoJSON polygon.
type"MultiPolygon"yesThe value identifies this record as a GeoJSON MultiPolygon.

GeoJSONPoint

A GeoJSON point is a GeoJSON geometry object of the type Point, as in RFC 7946.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
bboxlist of numberThis list contains the limits of the bounding box of the geometry, as in RFC 7946 section 5.
coordinatesGeoJSONPositionyesThis field gives the GeoJSON position of the point: longitude first, then latitude.
type"Point"yesThe value identifies this record as a GeoJSON Point.

GeoJSONPolygon

A GeoJSON polygon is a GeoJSON geometry object of the type Polygon, as in RFC 7946.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
bboxlist of numberThis list contains the limits of the bounding box of the geometry, as in RFC 7946 section 5.
coordinateslist of GeoJSONLinearRingyesThis list contains the linear rings of the polygon. The first ring is the outer boundary; the other rings are holes.
type"Polygon"yesThe value identifies this record as a GeoJSON Polygon.

GeoJSONPosition

A GeoJSON position is a longitude and a latitude in WGS 84 decimal degrees, in this sequence. A third number, the height, is optional. This sequence is the opposite of a geographic point.

Type: list of any

GeoPoint

A geographic point is a position in WGS 84 decimal degrees. An adapter is necessary for the Cartesian coordinates of a simulator.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
latitudenumberyesThis field gives the latitude north of the equator, in decimal degrees. A south latitude is a negative value.
longitudenumberyesThis field gives the longitude east of Greenwich, in decimal degrees. A west longitude is a negative value.

Geometry

Type: Geometry_point | Geometry_line | Geometry_polygon | Geometry_circle | Geometry_corridor | Geometry_racetrack | Geometry_track_racetrack | Geometry_sector | Geometry_polyarc | Geometry_path | Geometry_figure_eight | Geometry_vertical | Geometry_description | Geometry_geojson_point | Geometry_geojson_line | Geometry_geojson_polygon | Geometry_rectangle | Geometry_ellipse

Geometry_circle

A circle geometry is a horizontal disc with a centre and a radius.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
centerGeoPointyesThis field gives the geographic position of the centre of the circle, as latitude and longitude.
kind"circle"yesThe value identifies this record as a circle geometry. The value is circle.
radiusLengthyesThis field gives the horizontal distance from the centre to the boundary, as a length with its unit.

Geometry_corridor

A corridor geometry is a route centreline with a total lateral width.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
kind"corridor"yesThe value identifies this record as a corridor geometry. The value is corridor.
one_waybooleanThe value is true when aircraft fly the corridor only in the sequence of its points. The value is false when aircraft fly the corridor in the two directions.
pointslist of GeoPointyesThis list contains the geographic positions of the centreline, in order. The first position is the start.
widthLengthyesThis field gives the total lateral width of the corridor, with the centreline at its centre, as a length with its unit.

Geometry_description

A description geometry is a text that gives a geographic position or an area, with no coordinates.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
kind"description"yesThe value identifies this record as a description geometry. The value is description.
textstringyesThis field gives the geographic position or area, as free text.

Geometry_ellipse

An ellipse geometry is an ellipse with a centre in latitude and longitude and with dimensions in metres. It is not a polygon of sample points. A Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) drawing keeps its angle and its theatre projection in extensions.sim.dcs.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
centerGeoPointyesThis field gives the geographic position of the centre of the ellipse, as latitude and longitude.
east_radius_mnumberyesThis field gives the east radius before a simulator turns the drawing, in metres.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
kind"ellipse"yesThe value identifies this record as a ellipse geometry. The value is ellipse.
north_radius_mnumberyesThis field gives the north radius before a simulator turns the drawing, in metres.

Geometry_figure_eight

A figure-eight geometry is a figure-eight flight pattern with an anchor, an axis, a leg length and a turn radius.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
axisBearingyesThis field gives the direction of the axis of the flight pattern from its anchor, as a bearing with its unit and reference.
kind"figure_eight"yesThe value identifies this record as a figure-eight geometry. The value is figure_eight.
leg_lengthLengthyesThis field gives the length of each straight leg, without the turns, as a length with its unit.
pointGeoPointyesThis field gives the geographic position of the anchor of the flight pattern, as latitude and longitude.
turn_radiusLengthThis field gives the radius of the turns of the flight pattern, when given, as a length with its unit.

Geometry_geojson_line

A GeoJSON line geometry is a line as a GeoJSON geometry object (RFC 7946), unchanged. Shapes from a geographic information system (GIS) tool go in as they are. GeoJSON has no curves: circles, arcs and racetracks use their openAIX kinds.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
geometryGeoJSONLineStringyesThis field contains the GeoJSON LineString object.
kind"geojson"yesThe value identifies this record as a GeoJSON geometry. The value is geojson.

Geometry_geojson_point

A GeoJSON point geometry is a point as a GeoJSON geometry object (RFC 7946), unchanged. Shapes from a geographic information system (GIS) tool go in as they are. GeoJSON has no curves: circles, arcs and racetracks use their openAIX kinds.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
geometryGeoJSONPointyesThis field contains the GeoJSON Point object.
kind"geojson"yesThe value identifies this record as a GeoJSON geometry. The value is geojson.

Geometry_geojson_polygon

A GeoJSON polygon or multipolygon geometry is a polygon or multipolygon as a GeoJSON geometry object (RFC 7946), unchanged. Shapes from a geographic information system (GIS) tool go in as they are. GeoJSON has no curves: circles, arcs and racetracks use their openAIX kinds.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
geometryGeoJSONPolygon | GeoJSONMultiPolygonyesThis field contains the GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon object.
kind"geojson"yesThe value identifies this record as a GeoJSON geometry. The value is geojson.

Geometry_line

A line geometry is a sequence of geographic positions that makes an open line.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
kind"line"yesThe value identifies this record as a line geometry. The value is line.
pointslist of GeoPointyesThis list contains the geographic positions of the open line, in order. The first position is the start.

Geometry_path

A path geometry is an open line of straight segments and circular-arc segments in sequence. It does not close into an area.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
kind"path"yesThe value identifies this record as a path geometry. The value is path.
segmentslist of object | objectyesThis list contains, in order, the straight segments and circular-arc segments that make the path. A straight segment that follows a straight segment shall start at its end.

Geometry_point

A point geometry is one geographic position.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
kind"point"yesThe value identifies this record as a point geometry. The value is point.
positionGeoPointyesThis field gives the geographic position of the point, as latitude and longitude.

Geometry_polyarc

A polyarc geometry is a horizontal boundary of straight segments and circular-arc segments in sequence.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
kind"polyarc"yesThe value identifies this record as a polyarc geometry. The value is polyarc.
segmentslist of object | objectyesThis list contains, in order, the straight segments and circular-arc segments that make the boundary.

Geometry_polygon

A polygon geometry is a closed horizontal boundary. The first ring is the external boundary, and the next rings are holes.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
kind"polygon"yesThe value identifies this record as a polygon geometry. The value is polygon.
ringslist of list of GeoPointyesThis list contains the closed rings of positions, in order. The external boundary is first, and the holes come after it.

Geometry_racetrack

A racetrack geometry is a racetrack with an anchor, an outbound radial, a turn direction and a straight-leg length.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
kind"racetrack"yesThe value identifies this record as a racetrack geometry. The value is racetrack.
leg_lengthLengthyesThis field gives the length of each straight leg, without the turns, as a length with its unit.
pointGeoPointyesThis field gives the geographic position of the anchor of the racetrack, as latitude and longitude.
radialBearingyesThis field gives the outbound bearing from the anchor, as a bearing with its unit and reference. The reference is always given: true north or magnetic north. The reciprocal course is the course of the inbound leg.
turn_radiusLengthThis field gives the radius of the turns of the flight pattern, when given, as a length with its unit.
turnsenumyesThis field gives the direction of the turns around the flight pattern, as one of the enumerated values.
  • left
  • right

Geometry_rectangle

A rectangle geometry is a rectangle with a centre in latitude and longitude and with dimensions in metres. It is not a polygon of sample points. A Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) drawing keeps its angle and its theatre projection in extensions.sim.dcs.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
centerGeoPointyesThis field gives the geographic position of the centre of the rectangle, as latitude and longitude.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
height_mnumberyesThis field gives the height before a simulator turns the drawing, in metres.
kind"rectangle"yesThe value identifies this record as a rectangle geometry. The value is rectangle.
width_mnumberyesThis field gives the width before a simulator turns the drawing, in metres.

Geometry_sector

A sector geometry is a horizontal sector with a centre, a start bearing, an end bearing, and an inner and an outer radius.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
centerGeoPointyesThis field gives the geographic position of the centre of the sector, as latitude and longitude.
end_bearingBearingyesThis field gives the bearing of the second side of the sector, from its centre, as a bearing with its unit and reference.
inner_radiusLengthThis field gives the inner radius of the sector, as a length with its unit.
kind"sector"yesThe value identifies this record as a sector geometry. The value is sector.
outer_radiusLengthyesThis field gives the outer radius of the sector, as a length with its unit.
start_bearingBearingyesThis field gives the bearing of the first side of the sector, from its centre, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

Geometry_track_racetrack

A track racetrack geometry is a racetrack with two end anchors, a lateral width and a turn direction.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
aGeoPointyesThis field gives the geographic position of the first end anchor of the racetrack, as latitude and longitude.
bGeoPointyesThis field gives the geographic position of the second end anchor of the racetrack, as latitude and longitude.
kind"track_racetrack"yesThe value identifies this record as a track racetrack geometry. The value is track_racetrack.
turnsenumyesThis field gives the direction of the turns around the flight pattern, as one of the enumerated values.
  • left
  • right
widthLengthyesThis field gives the horizontal width of the racetrack, as a length with its unit.

Geometry_vertical

A vertical geometry is a coordination level, or the two values of a traverse level. The values of a traverse level are a height above the ground and an altitude above mean sea level.

Type: object | object

Hazard

A hazard is a danger to the aircraft in the target area that is not a threat.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
descriptionstringThis field gives the hazard, as free text.
kindenumyesThis field gives the type of hazard, as one of the enumerated values.
  • obstruction This value identifies an obstruction, such as a tower or a mast.
  • wires This value identifies wires or cables in the air.
  • terrain This value identifies high ground in or near the attack run.
  • friendly_aircraft This value identifies other friendly aircraft in the target area.
  • indirect_fire This value identifies friendly artillery, mortar or naval gun fire in the target area.
  • weather This value identifies a dangerous weather condition in the target area.
  • other This value identifies a hazard that the other values do not include.
positionGeoPointThis field gives the geographic position of the hazard, as latitude and longitude.

Identifier

Type: string

LaserCode

A laser code is a code of four digits for the pulse repetition frequency (PRF) of a laser, from 1111 to 1888. The digits after the first are 1 to 8. Most Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) aircraft and weapons accept only codes up to 1788; the comms standard check warns above it.

Type: string

Length

A length is a horizontal distance or dimension with its unit: metres, feet, nautical miles or kilometres.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
unitenumyesThis field gives the unit of the length: metres, feet, nautical miles or kilometres, as one of the enumerated values.
  • m
  • ft
  • nm
  • km
valuenumberyesThis field gives the value of the length, in the unit of unit.

LinkStation

A link 16 station number is a Link 16 station number (STN), which is five octal digits.

Type: string

MeasureCatalogue

Type: map of ControlMeasure

Metadata

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
authorstringThis field gives the name of the author of the document.
classificationClassificationLevelThis field gives the security classification of the document, as one of the enumerated values.
distributionlist of stringThis list contains the addressees that receive the document.
idstringyesThis field identifies this document. Other records and orders use it to refer to this document.
issued_atDateTimeThis field gives the time of issue of the document.
issuing_unitstringThis field gives the name of the unit that publishes the document.
operationstringThis field gives the name of the operation that the document is for.
referenceslist of DocumentRefThis list contains the documents that this document refers to.
revisionstringThis field gives the revision of the document.
supersedesDocumentRefThis field identifies the document that this document replaces.
titlestringThis field gives the title of the document.

Offset

An offset is a number of minutes from the start of the period of the air tasking order (ATO) that contains it. The value can be less than zero.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
offset_minutesnumberyesThis field gives the time from the start of the period of the air tasking order (ATO) that contains it, in minutes. A negative value is before the start of the period.

Period

A period is a time interval between two absolute date-times in the RFC 3339 format.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
endDateTimeyesThis field gives the time of the end of the period. The value is an absolute date-time.
startDateTimeyesThis field gives the time of the start of the period. The value is an absolute date-time.

PinnedRef

A pinned reference is a dependency on a local document that consumers examine by identifier and revision.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
idstringyesThis field identifies the local document of this dependency.
pathstringyesThis field gives the file path of the local document.
revisionstringyesThis field gives the revision of the local document. Consumers examine this revision.

PointLocation

A point location is a geographic point, a location in free text, or the two.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
positionGeoPointThis field gives the geographic position of the point, as latitude and longitude.
position_descriptionstringThis field gives the location, as free text. The text is for a location without accurate coordinates, or it gives more information about the coordinates.

Pressure

A pressure is an atmospheric pressure with its unit: inches of mercury or hectopascals.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
unitenumyesThis field gives the unit of the pressure: inches of mercury or hectopascals, as one of the enumerated values.
  • inHg The pressure is in inches of mercury.
  • hPa The pressure is in hectopascals.
valuenumberyesThis field gives the value of the pressure, in the unit of unit.

RadioAssignment

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
activitieslist of stringThis list identifies the flight operations that use this radio assignment. Each identifier shall refer to an item of activities of the flight. When the list is not given, the assignment is for the complete mission.
channelIdentifieryesThis field identifies the radio channel that this assignment uses.
presetintegerThis field gives the preset number of the radio channel on the radio of the aircraft.
purposestringThis field gives the operation or objective of this radio assignment, as free text.
radiostringThis field gives the radio of the aircraft that uses the channel, such as UHF or VHF, as free text.

ResourceRef

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies the external resource catalogue.
revisionstringyesThis field gives the revision of the external resource catalogue.

RunwayDesignator

A runway designator is the magnetic heading of the runway in units of 10 degrees, from 01 to 36. A suffix can follow: L, R or C for left, right or centre, or W for water. Other suffixes are S for short take-off and landing (STOL), G for glider and U for ultralight aircraft.

Type: string

ScheduledWindow

A scheduled window is a time interval between two absolute date-times, with a Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) schedule for each week in it.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
endstring (date-time)yesThis field gives the time of the end of the interval. The value is an absolute date-time.
scheduleWeeklyScheduleyesThis field gives the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) schedule for each week in the interval.
startstring (date-time)yesThis field gives the time of the start of the interval. The value is an absolute date-time.

SimData

Simulator data is the data of a record for each simulator, with the simulator identifier as the key, for example dcs. The other fields of the record do not change with a simulator. The Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) data has fixed fields, and the data of a different simulator is an object with no fixed fields.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
dcsDCSDataThis field contains the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) data of the record.

Speed

A speed is a speed with its unit: knots, Mach number or kilometres in one hour.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
unitenumyesThis field gives the unit of the speed: knots, Mach number or kilometres in one hour, as one of the enumerated values.
  • kt
  • mach
  • km/h
valuenumberyesThis field gives the value of the speed, in the unit of unit.

TACAN

A Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) is the channel, band and identifier of a TACAN station.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
bandenumyesThis field gives the band of the channel: X or Y, as one of the enumerated values.
  • X
  • Y
channelintegeryesThis field gives the channel number of the station, from 1 to 126.
identifierstringThis field identifies this station.

TargetMark

A target mark is the means that marks a target for the aircrew. The close air support (CAS) briefs of the air tasking order (ATO) and the operation order (OPORD) use this one list of values.

Type: enum

  • laser This value identifies a mark from a laser designator, which the seeker of the weapon or the targeting pod of the aircraft detects.
  • infrared_pointer This value identifies a mark from an infrared pointer. Aircrew with night vision devices can see it on the target.
  • smoke This value identifies a mark from smoke ammunition at or near the target.
  • white_phosphorus This value identifies a mark from white phosphorus ammunition at or near the target.
  • illumination This value identifies a mark from illumination ammunition above or near the target.
  • indirect_fire This value identifies a mark from artillery, mortar or naval gun fire.
  • tracer This value identifies a mark from tracer rounds, which show the line of fire to the target.
  • talk_on This value identifies a talk-on, in which the controller tells the aircrew how to find the target by voice.

VerticalLimit

A vertical limit is a floor or a ceiling: an altitude with its reference, the surface, or no limit. The surface is below all altitudes, and the value unlimited is above all altitudes.

Type: Altitude | object | object

WeeklyPeriod

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
end_day_offsetenumyesThis field gives the day on which the period stops, as one of the enumerated values. With the value 0, the period stops on its start day, and with 1, it stops on the next day.
  • 0
  • 1
end_timestringyesThis field gives the time of the end of the period, in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), as HH:MM:SS. The period does not include the end time.
start_timestringyesThis field gives the time of the start of the period, in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), as HH:MM:SS. The period includes the start time.
weekdayslist of enumyesThis list contains the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) weekdays on which this period starts.
  • mon
  • tue
  • wed
  • thu
  • fri
  • sat
  • sun

WeeklySchedule

A schedule for each week is the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) times in the week when something is available, in the interval that contains it. The intervals in exclusions are not part of the schedule.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
exclusionslist of objectThis list contains the time intervals with absolute date-times that the schedule subtracts from its periods.
periodslist of WeeklyPeriodyesThis list contains the time intervals in each week.
time_reference"UTC"yesThis field gives the time reference of the schedule. The value is always UTC.

Window

A window is a time interval with limits that are absolute date-times or offsets from the period of the order that contains it.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
endDateTime | OffsetyesThis field gives the time of the end of the interval. The value is an absolute date-time or an offset from the period of the order that contains it.
startDateTime | OffsetyesThis field gives the time of the start of the interval. The value is an absolute date-time or an offset from the period of the order that contains it.

Communications standard

urn:openaix:schema:comms-standard:0.2.0-draft.1

comms-standard

A communications standard is one force's standing plan for radio channels, Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN), Link 16 station numbers, identification codes and laser codes. It gives every value of every aircraft, and rules gives the patterns that the values follow. A consumer looks the values up and does not compute them.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastring (uri)This field identifies the schema that validates this document.
airfieldsAirfieldsThis field gives the rule for the beacons and channels of land airfields.
channelsmap of ChannelThis map contains the radio channels, which are the frequency ladder, the tanker and support channels and the flight channels. The key of each item is its identifier.
datalinkDatalinkThis field gives the Link 16 network and the rules for the team and the donors.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
flightsmap of FlightThis map contains the flights, which give the callsign, channels and the values of each member. The key of each item is its identifier.
iffIffThis field gives the default identification settings.
kind"comms_standard"yesThe value identifies this record as a communications standard.
laserLaserThis field gives the laser codes of the controllers, the blocks and the alternatives.
metaMetadatayesThis field gives the identification, revision and issue data of this communications standard.
radio_plansmap of RadioPlanThis map contains the radio plans, which give the presets of the radios of an aircraft type. The key of each item is its identifier.
restrictionsRestrictionsThis field gives the Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) channels, frequencies and identification codes that nothing uses.
ruleslist of RuleThis list contains the patterns that the values of the members follow. The check validates the tables against these patterns.
schema_version"0.2.0-draft.1"yesThis field gives the version of the openAIX schema that this communications standard agrees with.
shipsmap of ShipThis map contains the ships, which give the beacons and the channels of a ship. The key of each item is its identifier.
sourceslist of DocumentRefThis list contains the documents that the values of the standard come from.
squadronsmap of SquadronThis map contains the squadrons, which give the codes that a squadron shares. The key of each item is its identifier.
supportmap of SupportThis map contains the support aircraft: tankers and airborne early warning aircraft. The key of each item is its identifier.

Airfields

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
link4falseyesThe value is true when an airfield has Link 4. The value is false when an airfield has no Link 4.
overridesmap of FieldOverrideThis map contains the values that differ from the airfield record. The key of each item is its airfield identifier.
proposalslist of stringThis list contains the identifiers of the proposals that this airfield rule still carries, such as a1 or b11.
ruleenumyesThis field gives the rule that gives the beacons and the channels of an airfield, as one of the enumerated values.
  • airfield_record
sourceDocumentRefThis field identifies the source document. The reference gives the identifier of the document, and the path and the section give the file and the line.
statusStatusThis field gives the status of this airfield rule: the owner adopted its values, or only proposed them, as one of the enumerated values. A proposed value can change.

networkobjectyesThis field gives the Link 16 channels of the network.
proposalslist of stringThis list contains the identifiers of the proposals that this data link network still carries, such as a1 or b11.
sourceDocumentRefThis field identifies the source document. The reference gives the identifier of the document, and the path and the section give the file and the line.
statusStatusThis field gives the status of this data link network: the owner adopted its values, or only proposed them, as one of the enumerated values. A proposed value can change.
team_ruleenumThis field gives the rule that selects the team members of an aircraft, as one of the enumerated values.
  • flight_members

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
channelslist of IdentifierThis list identifies the radio channels that the airfield uses instead of the channels of the airfield record.

tacanTACANThis field gives the Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) channel of the airfield, when it differs from the airfield record.
