link4FrequencyyesThis field gives the link 4 frequency of the ship, as a frequency with its unit.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this ship, for display.
proposalslist of stringThis list contains the identifiers of the proposals that this ship still carries, such as a1 or b11.
radioIdentifierThis field identifies the radio channel that the ship uses for its control.
recovery_tankerIdentifierThis field identifies the support aircraft that is the recovery tanker of the ship.
sourceDocumentRefThis field identifies the source document. The reference gives the identifier of the document, and the path and the section give the file and the line.
standardbooleanThe value is true when the standard names this ship as the standard carrier. The value is false when the ship is supported but is not the standard carrier.
statusStatusThis field gives the status of this ship: the owner adopted its values, or only proposed them, as one of the enumerated values. A proposed value can change.
tacanTACANyesThis field gives the Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) channel of the ship.

Squadron

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
aircraft_typeIdentifieryesThis field gives the aircraft type of the squadron, as an identifier.
flightslist of IdentifierThis list identifies the flights that belong to this squadron.
midsobjectThis field gives the channels of the Link 16 voice nets of the squadron.
mode_1stringyesThis field gives the identification Mode 1 code of the squadron, as two octal digits.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this squadron, for display.
proposalslist of stringThis list contains the identifiers of the proposals that this squadron still carries, such as a1 or b11.
sourceDocumentRefThis field identifies the source document. The reference gives the identifier of the document, and the path and the section give the file and the line.
statusStatusThis field gives the status of this squadron: the owner adopted its values, or only proposed them, as one of the enumerated values. A proposed value can change.
stn_prefixstringyesThis field gives the first two octal digits of the Link 16 station numbers of the squadron.

Status

A status is whether the owner adopted the value of a record or only proposed it.

Type: enum

  • proposed

Support

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
aircraft_typeIdentifieryesThis field gives the aircraft type of the support aircraft, as an identifier.
callsignstringyesThis field gives the callsign of the support aircraft.

datalink_callsignstringyesThis field gives the callsign of the support aircraft in the data link, as two capital letters.
mode_1stringThis field gives the identification Mode 1 code of the support aircraft, as two octal digits.
mode_3stringyesThis field gives the identification Mode 3 code of the support aircraft, as four octal digits.
proposalslist of stringThis list contains the identifiers of the proposals that this support aircraft still carries, such as a1 or b11.
refuelenumThis field gives the refuelling method of the tanker, as one of the enumerated values.

roleenumyesThis field gives the role of the support aircraft, as one of the enumerated values.

sourceDocumentRefThis field identifies the source document. The reference gives the identifier of the document, and the path and the section give the file and the line.
statusStatusThis field gives the status of this support aircraft: the owner adopted its values, or only proposed them, as one of the enumerated values. A proposed value can change.
stnLinkStationyesThis field gives the Link 16 station number of the support aircraft.
tacanTACANyesThis field gives the Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) channel of the support aircraft.

leadTACANyesThis field gives the air-to-air Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) channel of the lead aircraft.
wingTACANyesThis field gives the air-to-air Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) channel of the wing aircraft.

TacanRestriction

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
bandenumyesThis field gives the band of the restricted channels, as one of the enumerated values.

Control measure

urn:openaix:schema:control-measure:0.2.0-draft.1

control-measure

A control measure is one of the openAIX control measure contracts, and its type selects the contract.

Type: ControlMeasure

Forward air controller

urn:openaix:schema:fac:0.2.0-draft.1

fac

A forward air controller (FAC) is a record of a FAC, a joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) or an airborne forward air controller (FAC(A)). It contains the role, the platform, the communications and the control functions of the controller.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastring (uri)This field identifies the schema that validates this document.
callsignstringyesThis field gives the radio call sign of the controller, as free text.
channelslist of IdentifierThis list identifies the radio channels that the controller uses.
coordinate_sourceenumThis field gives the method that the controller uses to get target coordinates, as one of the enumerated values. The value is not a type of target location error.
  • lrf This value identifies coordinates from a laser rangefinder at a known observer position.
  • visual This value identifies a visual estimate by the controller.
  • exact This value identifies accurate coordinates from the simulator.
default_laser_codeLaserCodeThis field gives the laser code that the controller uses when the brief gives no other code, as a laser code with its unit.
egress_pointslist of ControlMeasureSelectionThis list identifies the egress points that the controller gives to aircraft. Each one refers to a point with the role egress, gate or fix.
equipmentlist of objectThis list contains the equipment items that the controller or the observer team has. When an item is not in the list, the list does not add or remove that equipment.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record. The data in this field is for one consumer. The controller record keeps the data that all consumers can use. Examples are the identification, the equipment and the functions of the controller.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this controller. Other records and orders use it to refer to this controller.
initial_pointslist of ControlMeasureSelectionThis list identifies the initial points that the controller uses for attack briefs. Each one refers to a point with the role initial or fix.
kind"fac"yesThe value identifies this record as a forward air controller.
laser_codeslist of LaserCodeThis list contains the laser codes that the designators of the controller can use.
platformenumThis field gives the platform of the controller: on the ground (ground) or in an aircraft (airborne), as one of the enumerated values.
  • ground
  • airborne
positionGeoPointThis field gives the geographic position of the controller, as latitude and longitude.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the external resource catalogue that resolves the references of this record. The reference identifies the catalogue and gives its revision.
roleenumyesThis field gives the qualification of the controller, as one of the enumerated values. The controller is a forward air controller (FAC), a joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) or an airborne forward air controller (FAC(A)).
  • fac
  • jtac
  • fac_a
smoke_colorenumThis field gives the colour of the smoke that identifies targets or friendly positions, as one of the enumerated values.
  • white
  • red
  • green
  • orange
  • blue
terminal_controllist of enumThis list contains the types of terminal attack control that the controller may give.
  • type_1
  • type_2
  • type_3

Grid Minimum Off-Route Altitude (MORA)

urn:openaix:schema:grid-mora:0.2.0-draft.1

grid-mora

A grid of minimum off-route altitudes is a set of one-degree cells, each with its minimum off-route altitude (MORA). Each cell has one degree of latitude by one degree of longitude. A cell with an unknown value does not have the value zero.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
cellslist of CellyesThis list contains the one-degree cells. The list does not include cells without published data.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this record of a grid of minimum off-route altitudes. Other resources and orders use this stable identifier to refer to this record of a grid of minimum off-route altitudes.
kind"grid-mora"yesThe value identifies this record as a record of a grid of minimum off-route altitudes. The value selects this navigation contract.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this record of a grid of minimum off-route altitudes, for display.
provenanceProvenanceThis field gives the provenance of this record of a grid of minimum off-route altitudes as structured data: how the data were made, the authority, the aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle and the tool that made them.
sourcestringThis field gives the source of this record. The value gives the authority that publishes the data, and the cycle, for example FAA CIFP cycle 2610. A record that an author writes does not have this field. The field provenance gives the same facts as structured data.

Cell

A grid cell is one cell of the grid, with one degree of latitude and one degree of longitude. Its edges are on full degrees of latitude and longitude.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
minimum_altitudeAltitude & anyThis field gives the minimum off-route altitude (MORA) of the cell, above mean sea level, as an altitude with its unit and reference.
northeastGeoPointyesThis field gives the geographic position of the north-east corner of the cell, as latitude and longitude. This corner is one degree north and one degree east of the south-west corner.
southwestGeoPointyesThis field gives the geographic position of the south-west corner of the cell, as latitude and longitude.
statusenumyesThis field gives the condition of the minimum off-route altitude (MORA) of the cell, as one of the enumerated values. An unknown value is not zero.
  • known The source publishes a minimum off-route altitude (MORA) for the cell.
  • unknown The source identifies the minimum off-route altitude (MORA) of the cell as unknown. An unknown value is not zero.

Holding

urn:openaix:schema:holding:0.2.0-draft.1

holding

A hold record is a holding pattern at a fix. An author writes the hold for an air traffic control (ATC) holding stack, or a published holding leg of a procedure gives it.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
airfieldIdentifierThis field identifies the airfield of the hold. When the airfield has a list of its hold records, the list shall include this hold record.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
holdHoldyesThis field gives the holding pattern of this record. It has the same definition as the holding legs of a procedure.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this record of a hold. Other resources and orders use this stable identifier to refer to this record of a hold.
kind"holding"yesThe value identifies this record as a record of a hold. The value selects this navigation contract.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this record of a hold, for display.
provenanceProvenanceThis field gives the provenance of this record of a hold as structured data: how the data were made, the authority, the aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle and the tool that made them.
remarksRemarksThis list contains the notes of the chart of the procedure or of the hold, as free text.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this record of a hold. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
sourcestringThis field gives the source of this record. The value gives the authority that publishes the data, and the cycle, for example FAA CIFP cycle 2610. A record that an author writes does not have this field. The field provenance gives the same facts as structured data.

Joint Integrated Prioritized Target List (JIPTL)

urn:openaix:schema:jiptl:0.2.0-draft.1

jiptl

A joint integrated prioritized target list (JIPTL) is a list of the targets of all the force, in the sequence of their priority. Each entry identifies a target that the planners examine and gives its priority. An entry may also give the location, the necessary effect, the tasking and the coordination data.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastring (uri)This field identifies the schema that validates this document.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
kind"jiptl"yesThe value identifies this record as a joint integrated prioritized target list (JIPTL).
metaMetadataThis field gives the identification, revision and issue data of this list.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the external resource catalogue that resolves the references of the list. The reference identifies the catalogue and gives its revision.
schema_version"0.2.0-draft.1"This field gives the version of the openAIX schema that this joint integrated prioritized target list (JIPTL) agrees with.
targetslist of JIPTLTargetyesThis list contains the targets, in the sequence of their priority. Each entry identifies a target and gives its priority number. Number 1 is the highest priority.

EngagementMeans

An approved weapon system is a weapon system or an aircraft type that has clearance to engage the target, with its weapon.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
sclIdentifierThis field identifies the standard conventional load (SCL) that is the load of the aircraft.
storeIdentifierThis field identifies the store that is the weapon. When the entry gives a standard conventional load (SCL), the SCL shall contain the store.
systemstringyesThis field gives the weapon system or type of aircraft, such as F-15E, M777 or HIMARS, as free text.

JIPTLTarget

A target entry is an entry for one target on a joint integrated prioritized target list (JIPTL), with its identification and priority. The optional fields give the location, the necessary effect, the component with the task and the weapon systems.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
authorized_engagement_meanslist of EngagementMeansThis list contains the weapon systems that have clearance to engage the target. Each entry gives the system, and can refer to the standard conventional load (SCL) and the weapon in the resource catalogue.
component_taskedenumThis field gives the component of the joint force that has the task to prosecute this target, as one of the enumerated values.
  • land
  • air
  • maritime
  • sof
  • cyber
  • space
desired_effectenumThis field gives the effect on the target that the commander wants, as one of the enumerated values.
  • destroy
  • neutralize
  • suppress
  • disrupt
  • degrade
  • deny
  • divert
locationGeoPointThis field gives the geographic position of the target at the time of approval, as latitude and longitude. A producer updates the position after a dynamic retasking.
location_mgrsstringThis field gives the same position for display, in the Military Grid Reference System (MGRS), as free text. If the two values are different, the geographic position has priority.
priority_rankintegeryesThis field gives the priority number of the target on the joint integrated prioritized target list (JIPTL). Number 1 is the highest priority.
statusenumThis field gives the lifecycle condition of the target at this time, as one of the enumerated values.
  • approved
  • pending
  • denied
  • executed
  • expired
targetIdentifierThis field identifies the target that is this entry, in the resource catalogue.
target_descriptionstringThis field gives the data that tells the type of the target and how it is important, as free text.
target_namestringThis field gives the name of this target, for display. The name is short, for example ENY MRC CP, OBJ HAMMER.
target_numberstringyesThis field identifies this target. The value is a basic encyclopedia number, such as BE-0042-01, or a local number, such as TGT 0042.

Localizer

urn:openaix:schema:localizer:0.2.0-draft.1

localizer

A localizer is the transmitter of an instrument landing system (ILS) that shows the lateral position of the aircraft in relation to the course. The record has its frequency, its course and, when the ILS has one, its glide slope.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
airfieldIdentifierThis field identifies the airfield of the localizer. When the airfield has a list of its localizers, the list shall include this localizer.
courseBearingyesThis field gives the front course of the localizer, as a bearing with its unit and reference. A magnetic course includes the station declination, which is more than zero for east.
elevationElevationThis field gives the elevation of the localizer antenna above mean sea level, as an elevation with its unit.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
frequencyFrequency & anyyesThis field gives the frequency of the localizer, as a frequency with its unit. The unit is megahertz.
glide_slopeGlideSlopeThis field gives the glide slope transmitter for the same runway, when the runway has one.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this localizer. Other resources and orders use this stable identifier to refer to this localizer.
identstringThis field identifies this localizer as the station transmits it in Morse code. An example is IDQQ.
ils_categoryenumThis field gives the instrument landing system (ILS) Category of the localizer, as one of the enumerated values. A localizer without a glide slope does not have this field.
  • I This value identifies an instrument landing system (ILS) for approaches with a decision height of 200 feet or more.
  • II This value identifies an instrument landing system (ILS) for approaches with a decision height from 100 feet to less than 200 feet.
  • III This value identifies an instrument landing system (ILS) for approaches with a decision height of less than 100 feet, or with no decision height.
kind"localizer"yesThe value identifies this record as a localizer record. The value selects this navigation contract.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this localizer, for display.
positionGeoPointyesThis field gives the geographic position of the localizer antenna, as latitude and longitude.
provenanceProvenanceThis field gives the provenance of this localizer as structured data: how the data were made, the authority, the aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle and the tool that made them.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this localizer. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
runwayRunwayDesignatorThis field gives the designator of the runway of the localizer.
sourcestringThis field gives the source of this record. The value gives the authority that publishes the data, and the cycle, for example FAA CIFP cycle 2610. A record that an author writes does not have this field. The field provenance gives the same facts as structured data.
systemenumThis field gives the landing system that the localizer belongs to, as one of the enumerated values. A record without this field is the localizer of an instrument landing system (ILS).
  • ils This value identifies the instrument landing system (ILS) of International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Annex 10: a localizer with an optional glide slope.
  • prmg This value identifies the landing radio beacon group (PRMG): the landing system of the Soviet Union and Russia. It gives a front course and a glide slope to a runway as an instrument landing system (ILS) does, with its own signals and its own channel numbers.
threshold_crossing_heightLengthThis field gives the threshold crossing height (TCH) of the glide slope, as a length with its unit. It is the height of the glide slope above the landing threshold.

GlideSlope

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
angle_degnumberyesThis field gives the angle between the glide path and a horizontal line, in degrees.
elevationElevationThis field gives the elevation of the glide slope antenna above mean sea level, as an elevation with its unit.
positionGeoPointThis field gives the geographic position of the glide slope antenna, as latitude and longitude. A source that does not publish the position of the antenna leaves this field out.

Minimum Safe Altitude (MSA)

urn:openaix:schema:msa:0.2.0-draft.1

msa

A minimum safe altitude (MSA) is the minimum altitudes in sectors around a centre fix, in the radius of the sectors. The bearings of a sector are bearings to the centre. Each sector goes in the clockwise direction from the bearing at its start to the bearing at its end.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
airfieldIdentifierThis field identifies the airfield of this record. An example is kden.
centerFixyesThis field gives the fix at the centre of the sectors: a navigation aid, a waypoint or an airport reference point.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this record of a minimum safe altitude. Other resources and orders use this stable identifier to refer to this record of a minimum safe altitude.
kind"msa"yesThe value identifies this record as a record of a minimum safe altitude. The value selects this navigation contract.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this record of a minimum safe altitude, for display.
provenanceProvenanceThis field gives the provenance of this record of a minimum safe altitude as structured data: how the data were made, the authority, the aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle and the tool that made them.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this record of a minimum safe altitude. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
sectorslist of SectoryesThis list contains the sectors around the centre. Together, the sectors make the full circle. Each sector goes in the clockwise direction from the bearing at its start to the bearing at its end.
sourcestringThis field gives the source of this record. The value gives the authority that publishes the data, and the cycle, for example FAA CIFP cycle 2610. A record that an author writes does not have this field. The field provenance gives the same facts as structured data.

Sector

A minimum safe altitude (MSA) sector is one sector around the centre fix. Its bearings are bearings to the centre, as the chart shows them, and they are usually magnetic. The sector goes in the clockwise direction from start_bearing to end_bearing.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
end_bearingBearingyesThis field gives the bearing to the centre at the end of the sector, as a bearing with its unit and reference. It is equal to start_bearing only for a full circle.
full_circlebooleanyesThe value is true when this one sector is the full circle. Then, equal bearings do not identify a sector of zero width.
minimum_altitudeAltitude & anyyesThis field gives the minimum safe altitude (MSA) in the sector, above mean sea level, as an altitude with its unit and reference.
radiusLengthyesThis field gives the radius of the sector from the centre, as a length with its unit.
start_bearingBearingyesThis field gives the bearing to the centre at the start of the sector, as a bearing with its unit and reference. From this bearing, the sector goes in the clockwise direction.

Navigation aid

urn:openaix:schema:navaid:0.2.0-draft.1

navaid

A navigation aid (NAVAID) is a radio navigation facility. The record has its equipment class, its position, and its frequency or the channel of its Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN).

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
airfieldIdentifierThis field identifies the airfield at which the navigation aid is. When the airfield has a list of its navigation aids, the list shall include this navigation aid.
classenumyesThis field gives the equipment class of the navigation aid, as one of the enumerated values.
  • VOR This value identifies a VOR station. Its very high frequency (VHF) signal gives the aircraft its magnetic bearing from the station.
  • VOR_DME This value identifies a VOR station with a DME at the same site. It gives the aircraft its bearing from the station and its slant distance to the station.
  • VORTAC This value identifies a VORTAC station: a VOR and a TACAN at one site. Aircraft of civil aviation use the VOR, and aircraft of armed forces use the TACAN.
  • TACAN This value identifies a TACAN station. On ultra high frequency (UHF), it gives aircraft of armed forces their magnetic bearing and slant distance from the station.
  • DME This value identifies a DME station. It gives the aircraft its slant distance to the station.
  • NDB This value identifies an NDB station. It transmits a signal in all directions. A direction finder in the aircraft shows the direction to the station.
  • NDB_DME This value identifies an NDB station with a DME at the same site. It gives the direction to the station and the slant distance to the station. The frequency of the record is the frequency of the NDB.
  • ILS_DME This value identifies a DME that operates with the localizer of an instrument landing system (ILS).
  • MARKER This value identifies a marker beacon. It transmits a signal on 75 MHz in a vertical fan above the beacon. It marks a point on the approach path, for example the outer marker of an instrument landing system (ILS).
  • RSBN This value identifies an RSBN station: the short-range radio navigation system of the Soviet Union and Russia. It gives the aircraft its azimuth and slant range from the station on ultra high frequency (UHF), as TACAN does.
dme_positionGeoPointThis field gives the geographic position of the distance measuring equipment (DME) antenna, as latitude and longitude. The record has this field when the source publishes this position. A station with only a DME or only a Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) does not always have a second position.
elevationElevationThis field gives the elevation of the distance measuring equipment (DME) antenna above mean sea level, as an elevation with its unit.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
frequencyFrequencyThis field gives the frequency of the station, as a frequency with its unit. The unit is kilohertz for a non-directional beacon (NDB) or an NDB with a distance measuring equipment (DME). For the other classes, the unit is megahertz. A station with only a Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) has no frequency. A marker beacon can leave the frequency out.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this navigation aid. Other resources and orders use this stable identifier to refer to this navigation aid.
identstringThis field identifies this navigation aid as the station transmits it in Morse code.
magnetic_variation_degnumberThis field gives the station declination, in degrees. The declination is the magnetic variation that the station uses to align its radials. Values for east are more than zero, and values for west are less than zero.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this navigation aid, for display.
positionGeoPointThis field gives the geographic position of the VOR, NDB or TACAN station, as latitude and longitude.
provenanceProvenanceThis field gives the provenance of this navigation aid as structured data: how the data were made, the authority, the aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle and the tool that made them.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this navigation aid. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
sourcestringThis field gives the source of this record. The value gives the authority that publishes the data, and the cycle, for example FAA CIFP cycle 2610. A record that an author writes does not have this field. The field provenance gives the same facts as structured data.
tacanTACANThis field gives the channel and the band of the Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) of the station. For a VORTAC, it is the channel that the distance measuring equipment (DME) channel pairing table gives for the VOR frequency.
type"NAVAID"yesThe value identifies this record as a control measure for a navigation aid, with the catalogue code NAVAID. The value selects this contract in a catalogue of control measures.

Notice to air missions (NOTAM)

urn:openaix:schema:notam:0.2.0-draft.1

notam

Notice to air missions (NOTAM) are a notice about the establishment, condition or change of an aeronautical facility, service, procedure or hazard. This record has the basic items of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) NOTAM format of Annex 15: the number, the location, the NOTAM Code, the effective time interval, the text and the vertical limits. Planners write NOTAMs before the operation.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
affectslist of ControlMeasureSelection | RunwaySelection | ProcedureSelectionThis list contains the runways, navigation aids, airspace and instrument procedures that the notice to air missions (NOTAM) is about. Each item is a runway end of the location, a control measure or an instrument procedure. A runway shall be an end of a runway of the location.
codestringyesThis field gives the notice to air missions (NOTAM) Code of item Q: the letter Q, two letters for the subject and two letters for its condition, for example QMRLC for a closed runway. International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Doc 8126 gives the NOTAM Code.
effectiveWindowyesThis field gives the time interval during which the notice to air missions (NOTAM) is in effect. It is items B and C of the NOTAM.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this notice to air missions (NOTAM). Other resources and orders use this stable identifier to refer to this NOTAM.
kind"notam"yesThe value identifies this record as a notice to air missions (NOTAM) record. The value selects this contract.
locationIdentifieryesThis field identifies the operating location that the notice to air missions (NOTAM) is about. It is item A of the NOTAM.
lowerVerticalLimitThis field gives the floor of the area that the notice to air missions (NOTAM) is about: an altitude with its reference, the surface or no limit. It is item F of the NOTAM.
numberNotamNumberyesThis field gives the notice to air missions (NOTAM) number: the series, the number in the series and the year. An example is A0123/26.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this notice to air missions (NOTAM). The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
textstringyesThis field gives the text of the notice to air missions (NOTAM), in the abbreviations of the NOTAM, as free text. It is item E of the NOTAM.
upperVerticalLimitThis field gives the ceiling of the area that the notice to air missions (NOTAM) is about: an altitude with its reference, the surface or no limit. It is item G of the NOTAM.

NotamNumber

A notice to air missions (NOTAM) number is the series letter, the number and the year that identify a NOTAM.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
numberintegeryesThis field gives the number of the notice to air missions (NOTAM) in its series and year, from 1 to 9999.
seriesstringyesThis field gives the series letter of the notice to air missions (NOTAM), for example A, as free text.
yearintegeryesThis field gives the year of the notice to air missions (NOTAM), with four digits. The NOTAM number shows its last two digits.

ProcedureSelection

A procedure selection is a reference to one instrument procedure of the resource catalogue.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies the instrument procedure that the notice to air missions (NOTAM) is about.
kind"instrument_procedure"yesThe value identifies this record as an instrument procedure selection.

RunwaySelection

A runway selection is a reference to one runway end of the location of the notice to air missions (NOTAM).

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
designatorRunwayDesignatoryesThis field gives the designator of the runway end, for example 03L.
kind"runway"yesThe value identifies this record as a runway selection.

Orbit

urn:openaix:schema:orbit:0.2.0-draft.1

orbit

An orbit is a flight pattern with an altitude block and the times when it is active. More than one assignment can use the same orbit. An airspace control order (ACO) assignment gives the mission role: combat air patrol (CAP), airborne early warning (AEW), air-to-air refuelling or holding. The orbit has no role.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
activeActivationyesThis field gives the time interval during which this orbit is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.
altitudeAltitudeBlockyesThis field gives the vertical limits of the orbit, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling. The block gives the altitudes that aircraft can use.
channelslist of IdentifierThis list identifies the communications channels of this orbit.
controlling_agencyIdentifierThis field identifies the agency that controls the operations in this orbit.
coordination_instructionslist of stringThis list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this orbit has an effect on.
descriptionstringThis field gives the information about this orbit and its local conditions, as free text.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
geometryGeometry_circle | Geometry_racetrack | Geometry_track_racetrack | Geometry_figure_eight | Geometry_line | Geometry_point | Geometry_description | Geometry_geojson_line | Geometry_geojson_pointyesThis field gives the horizontal geometry of the flight pattern. A racetrack has an anchor, a radial, a turn direction and a straight-leg length. A point, a line or a text geometry can record a pattern, but more data is necessary to fly it. A geojson geometry (RFC 7946) of the same shape is also correct.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this orbit. Other records and orders use it to refer to this orbit.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this orbit, for display.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about this orbit, as free text.
purposestringThis field gives the general task of the orbit, as free text.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this orbit. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
restrictionslist of stringThis list contains the conditions that control the operations in this orbit.
type"ORBIT"yesThe value identifies this record as an orbit. The value is the same for all orbits, and the mission of an assignment does not change it.

Path point

urn:openaix:schema:path-point:0.2.0-draft.1

path-point

A path point is the geometry of the final approach segment of an approach that uses satellite navigation. It has the landing threshold point (LTP), the flight path alignment point (FPAP), the glide path angle and the threshold crossing height (TCH).

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
airfieldIdentifierThis field identifies the airfield of this record. An example is kden.
approachstringThis field identifies the approach procedure. An example is R16RY.
approach_typestringThis field gives the published type of the approach, for example LPV or LP.
course_width_at_thresholdLengthThis field gives the course width at the landing threshold point (LTP), as a length with its unit. It is the lateral distance from the course centreline at which full-scale deflection occurs.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
final_approach_courseBearingThis field gives the final approach course, as a bearing with its unit and reference.
flight_path_alignment_pointGeoPointyesThis field gives the geographic position of the flight path alignment point (FPAP), as latitude and longitude. With the landing threshold point (LTP), this point gives the direction of the final approach course.
glide_path_angle_degnumberyesThis field gives the angle between the glide path and a horizontal line, in degrees.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this path point. Other resources and orders use this stable identifier to refer to this path point.
kind"path-point"yesThe value identifies this record as a path point record. The value selects this navigation contract.
landing_threshold_elevationElevationThis field gives the orthometric height of the landing threshold point (LTP) above mean sea level, as an elevation with its unit.
landing_threshold_pointGeoPointyesThis field gives the geographic position of the landing threshold point (LTP), as latitude and longitude. The path of the final approach goes above this point at the threshold crossing height.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this path point, for display.
provenanceProvenanceThis field gives the provenance of this path point as structured data: how the data were made, the authority, the aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle and the tool that made them.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this path point. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
runwayRunwayDesignatorThis field gives the designator of the runway of the approach.
sourcestringThis field gives the source of this record. The value gives the authority that publishes the data, and the cycle, for example FAA CIFP cycle 2610. A record that an author writes does not have this field. The field provenance gives the same facts as structured data.
threshold_crossing_heightLengthyesThis field gives the threshold crossing height (TCH) of the path of the final approach, as a length with its unit. It is the height of the path of the final approach above the landing threshold point (LTP).

Navigation or control point

urn:openaix:schema:point:0.2.0-draft.1

point

A point is a position with a name, for navigation or control. The roles tell how aircraft use the point, for example for ingress, egress, initial approach, contact point and handover. The air reference points of Annex B (ACP, CP, EG, HG, MG, ISP) are points with the applicable role. The initial point, the bullseye, a target reference point and a fire support station are also points with the applicable role. A charted reporting point for visual flight rules (VFR) flights is a point with the role visual_reporting.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
activeActivationyesThis field gives the time interval during which this point is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.
altitudeAltitudeBlockThis field gives the vertical limits of the point, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling. An example is the altitude block of an entry or exit gate in an airspace control order (ACO).
aorIdentifierThis field identifies the area of responsibility that this gate is for.
channelslist of IdentifierThis list identifies the communications channels of this point.
contact_agencyIdentifierThis field identifies the agency that aircraft speak to at this point.
coordination_instructionslist of stringThis list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this point has an effect on.
descriptionstringThis field gives the information about this point and its local conditions, as free text.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
handover_agencyIdentifierThis field identifies the agency that controls the aircraft after this gate.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this point. Other records and orders use it to refer to this point.
instructionslist of stringThis list contains the instructions for operations at this point.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this point, for display.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about this point, as free text.
positionPointLocation.positionThis field gives the geographic position of the point, as latitude and longitude.
position_descriptionPointLocation.position_descriptionThis field gives the location, as free text. The text is for a location without accurate coordinates, or it gives more information about the coordinates.
reference_agencyIdentifierThis field identifies the agency for this point or line.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this point. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
restrictionslist of stringThis list contains the conditions that control the operations in this point.
roleslist of enumyesThis list contains the roles of this point in operations. One point can have more than one role.
  • control
  • initial
  • ingress
  • egress
  • gate
  • handover
  • marshalling
  • identification_safety
  • bullseye
  • fix
  • target_reference
  • fire_support_station
  • visual_reporting
  • search_and_rescue
  • push
  • rendezvous
  • anchor
  • hold
routeIdentifierThis field identifies the route of this task or connection.
type"POINT"yesThe value identifies this record as a point control measure. This value is the same for all roles of a point.

Procedure

urn:openaix:schema:procedure:0.2.0-draft.1

procedure

An instrument procedure is a standard instrument departure (SID), a standard terminal arrival route (STAR) or an approach. It is a sequence of legs with altitude constraints and speed constraints.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
airfieldIdentifierThis field identifies the airfield at the start or at the end of the procedure. When the airfield has a list of its procedures, the list shall include this procedure.
approach_typeenumThis field gives the guidance of the final approach segment of an approach, as one of the enumerated values. Only an approach shall have this field. A par or asr approach shall have radar_approach, and other procedures shall not have it.
  • ils This value identifies an instrument landing system (ILS) approach, with a localizer and a glide slope.
  • localizer This value identifies a localizer approach, with lateral guidance from a localizer and no glide slope.
  • gls This value identifies a ground-based augmentation system landing system (GLS) approach, with lateral and vertical guidance from a ground-based augmentation system (GBAS) ground station.
  • rnav This value identifies an area navigation (RNAV) or required navigation performance (RNP) approach with satellite navigation, for example RNAV (GPS) or RNP.
  • vor This value identifies an approach with lateral guidance from a very high frequency omnidirectional range (VOR) station, with or without distance measuring equipment (DME).
  • tacan This value identifies an approach with lateral guidance from a Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) station.
  • ndb This value identifies an approach with guidance from a non-directional beacon (NDB) station.
  • par This value identifies a precision approach radar (PAR) approach: a controller gives the course and the glide path from a precision radar.
  • asr This value identifies an airport surveillance radar (ASR) approach: a controller gives the course and recommended altitudes from a surveillance radar.
climb_gradientslist of ClimbGradientThis list contains the minimum climb gradients of a departure or of the missed approach of an approach. An arrival shall not have this field.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
holdingslist of IdentifierThis list identifies the hold records of the procedure that the aircraft can fly on the procedure. When a hold record identifies an airfield, that airfield shall be the airfield of the procedure.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this procedure. Other resources and orders use this stable identifier to refer to this procedure.
identstringThis field identifies this procedure as published. An example is I16R.
kind"procedure"yesThe value identifies this record as a procedure record. The value selects this navigation contract.
minimalist of MinimaLineThis list contains the published minima lines of the approach. Only an approach shall have this field.
msaIdentifierThis field identifies the record of a minimum safe altitude that the chart of the procedure shows. When the record identifies an airfield, that airfield shall be the airfield of the procedure.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this procedure, for display.
navigation_specificationNavigationSpecificationThis field gives the navigation specification of the procedure: conventional navigation, area navigation (RNAV) or required navigation performance (RNP), and the sensors and navigation aids that it needs.
obstacle_assessmentObstacleAssessmentThis field gives the result of the obstacle clearance assessment of the procedure, segment by segment.
procedure_typeenumThis field gives the type of the procedure, as one of the enumerated values.
  • departure This value identifies a standard instrument departure (SID): an instrument flight rules (IFR) route from the runway to the en-route structure.
  • arrival This value identifies a standard terminal arrival route (STAR): an instrument flight rules (IFR) route from the en-route structure to the approach.
  • approach This value identifies an instrument approach procedure, from the initial approach fix to a landing or a missed approach.
provenanceProvenanceThis field gives the provenance of this procedure as structured data: how the data were made, the authority, the aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle and the tool that made them.
radar_approachRadarApproachThis field gives the final approach of a precision approach radar (PAR) or an airport surveillance radar (ASR) approach: the runway, the course, the glide path and the radar coverage.
remarksRemarksThis list contains the notes of the chart of the procedure or of the hold, as free text.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this procedure. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
runwayslist of RunwayDesignatorThis list contains the designators of the runway ends that the procedure serves. A standard instrument departure (SID) or a standard terminal arrival route (STAR) can serve several runways, and an approach serves the runway of its final approach course. When the airfield has runways, each designator shall be the designator of an end of a runway of the airfield.
sourcestringThis field gives the source of this record. The value gives the authority that publishes the data, and the cycle, for example FAA CIFP cycle 2610. A record that an author writes does not have this field. The field provenance gives the same facts as structured data.
takeoff_minimalist of TakeoffMinimumThis list contains the takeoff minima of a departure. Only a departure shall have this field.
threshold_crossing_heightLengthThis field gives the threshold crossing height (TCH) of the vertical path of the approach, as a length with its unit. It is the height of the vertical path above the landing threshold, for an approach with vertical guidance. A precision approach radar (PAR) or airport surveillance radar (ASR) approach gives its TCH in radar_approach. Only an approach other than a par or asr approach shall have this field.
top_altitudeAltitudeThis field gives the highest altitude that the departure publishes: the altitude at which the departure ends, as an altitude with its unit and reference. Only a departure shall have this field.
transitionslist of TransitionThis list contains the transitions and common route segments of the procedure. A transition without an identifier is the common route or the final approach. A procedure shall have this field, except a par or asr approach.

CategoryMinimum

A category minimum is the minima of a minima line for one or more aircraft approach categories. It has a decision altitude or a minimum descent altitude (MDA), a height and a visibility or a runway visual range (RVR).

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
categorieslist of enumyesThis list contains the aircraft approach categories to which these minima apply. Categories A to E follow the speed at the threshold, and category H is for helicopters.
  • A
  • B
  • C
  • D
  • E
  • H
decision_altitudeAltitude & anyThis field gives the decision altitude above mean sea level, as an altitude with its unit and reference. At this altitude the pilot starts the missed approach when the required visual references are not visible. The minima shall have this field or minimum_descent_altitude, but not both.
heightLengthThis field gives the height of the decision altitude or the minimum descent altitude (MDA) above the elevation that height_reference of the line names, as a length with its unit. For a decision altitude, this height is the decision height.
minimum_descent_altitudeAltitude & anyThis field gives the minimum descent altitude (MDA) above mean sea level, as an altitude with its unit and reference. The aircraft does not descend below this altitude without the required visual references.
runway_visual_rangeLength & anyThis field gives the minimum runway visual range (RVR) for the approach, as a length with its unit. The unit is feet or metres.
visibilityVisibilityThis field gives the minimum visibility for the approach, as a visibility with its unit.

ClimbGradient

A climb gradient is a minimum climb gradient of a departure or a missed approach. The aircraft climbs at this gradient or more until the altitude in until or the fix in until_fix.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
gradientGradientyesThis field gives the minimum climb gradient, as a gradient with its unit.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about the climb gradient, as free text.
reasonenumyesThis field gives the reason for the climb gradient, as one of the enumerated values.
  • obstacle This value identifies a gradient that keeps the obstacle clearance above the obstacles under the climb.
  • atc This value identifies a gradient that air traffic control (ATC) needs for airspace or for separation from other traffic.
runwayRunwayDesignatorThis field gives the designator of the departure runway of the climb gradient.
untilAltitude & anyThis field gives the altitude above mean sea level up to which the climb gradient applies, as an altitude with its unit and reference. The climb gradient shall have this field or until_fix.
until_fixFixThis field gives the fix up to which the climb gradient applies.

Duration

A time interval is a time interval in minutes.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
unit"min"yesThis field gives the unit of the time interval: minutes.
valuenumberyesThis field gives the number of minutes.

Fix

A fix is a navigation fix: its published identifier and position, or a reference to a point, a navigation aid or a localizer in the resource catalogue.

Type: object | ControlMeasureSelection | LocalizerSelection

Gradient

A gradient is a climb gradient with its unit.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
unitenumyesThis field gives the unit of the gradient, as one of the enumerated values.
  • ft/nm This value identifies a gradient in feet of climb for each nautical mile of distance.
  • percent This value identifies a gradient as a percentage of vertical climb to horizontal distance.
valuenumberyesThis field gives the value of the gradient, in the unit of unit.

Hold

A hold is a holding pattern with a fix, an inbound course, a turn direction, and a leg length or a leg time. Altitude constraints and speed constraints are optional.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
altitudeany & any & anyThis field gives the altitude constraint for the hold.
fixFixyesThis field gives the fix of the holding pattern.
inbound_courseBearingyesThis field gives the course of the inbound leg to the holding fix, as a bearing with its unit and reference.
leg_lengthLengthThis field gives the length of each holding leg, as a length with its unit. When the hold has this length, it does not have a leg time.
leg_timeDurationThis field gives the flight time of each holding leg, in minutes. When the hold has this time, it does not have a leg length.
speedSpeedConstraintThis field gives the speed constraint for the hold.
turn_directionenumyesThis field gives the direction of the turns in the holding pattern, as one of the enumerated values.
  • left Each turn is a left turn. This is not the standard holding pattern.
  • right Each turn is a right turn. This is the standard holding pattern.

Leg

A leg is one leg of a procedure: a path and the point at the end of the path. For each leg type, conditional rules make sure that the leg has the necessary data.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
altitudeany & any & any & anyThis field gives the altitude constraint at the end of the leg.
approach_fixlist of enumThis list contains the approach functions of the fix of the leg. A fix can have more than one function, for example the initial approach fix and the intermediate fix.
  • initial_approach_fix
  • intermediate_fix
  • final_approach_course_fix
  • final_approach_fix
  • missed_approach_point
  • stepdown_fix
  • missed_approach_holding_fix
arc_centerFixThis field gives the fix at the centre of the constant-radius arc of a radius_to_fix leg. A radius_to_fix leg shall have this field.
arc_radiusLengthThis field gives the radius of the constant-radius arc of a radius_to_fix leg, as a length with its unit. A radius_to_fix leg shall have this field.
courseBearingThis field gives the course, the track or the heading of the aircraft on the leg, as a bearing with its unit and reference. The reference is magnetic north or true north.
distanceLengthThis field gives the published distance of the leg, as a length with its unit.
fixFixThis field gives the fix at the end of the leg. For fix_to_altitude, track_from_fix_for_distance, track_from_fix_to_dme_distance, fix_to_manual_termination and procedure_turn legs, it is the fix at the start of the leg.
fly_overbooleanThe value is true when the aircraft is above the fix before it turns onto the next leg. The value is false when the aircraft starts the turn before the fix, as at a fly-by fix.
holdHoldThis field gives the holding pattern that the aircraft flies on a hold_to_altitude, hold_to_fix or hold_to_manual_termination leg. The hold has the fix, the course, the altitude constraint and the speed constraint of the leg. Other leg types shall not have this field.
leg_typeenumyesThis field gives the type of the leg, as one of the enumerated values. The type gives the path that the aircraft flies and the point at the end of the leg. Each value is a path terminator, and the text of the value gives its code of two letters. An example is track_to_fix, which has the code TF.
  • initial_fix This value identifies an initial fix (IF). The procedure or the transition in the procedure data starts at this fix. The leg has no path.
  • track_to_fix This value identifies a track to a fix (TF). The aircraft flies a straight track from the previous fix to the fix of the leg.
  • course_to_fix This value identifies a course to a fix (CF). The aircraft flies a given course to the fix of the leg.
  • direct_to_fix This value identifies a direct-to-fix leg (DF). The aircraft flies directly from its position to the fix of the leg.
  • fix_to_altitude This value identifies a course from a fix to an altitude (FA). The aircraft flies a given course from the fix of the leg. The aircraft completes the leg when it is at or above a given altitude.
  • track_from_fix_for_distance This value identifies a track from a fix for a distance (FC). From the fix of the leg, the aircraft flies the track over the ground of the leg for a given distance.
  • track_from_fix_to_dme_distance This value identifies a track from a fix to a distance measuring equipment (DME) distance (FD). The aircraft flies the track over the ground of the leg from the fix of the leg. The aircraft completes the leg at a given DME distance from a navigation aid.
  • fix_to_manual_termination This value identifies a course from a fix to a manual termination (FM). The aircraft flies a given course from the fix of the leg until a manual termination by the pilot, usually to fly a radar vector.
  • course_to_altitude This value identifies a course to an altitude (CA). The aircraft flies a given course. The aircraft completes the leg when it is at or above a given altitude, at no given position.
  • course_to_dme_distance This value identifies a course to a distance measuring equipment (DME) distance (CD). The aircraft flies a given course to a given DME distance from a navigation aid.
  • course_to_intercept This value identifies a course to intercept the next leg (CI). The aircraft flies a given course until it intercepts the next leg.
  • course_to_radial This value identifies a course to a radial (CR). The aircraft flies a given course to a given radial of a very high frequency omnidirectional range (VOR).
  • radius_to_fix This value identifies a radius to a fix (RF). The aircraft flies a constant-radius arc around a given centre, from the previous fix to the fix of the leg.
  • arc_to_fix This value identifies an arc to a fix (AF). The aircraft flies an arc at one distance measuring equipment (DME) distance from a navigation aid to the fix of the leg.
  • heading_to_altitude This value identifies a heading to an altitude (VA). The aircraft flies a given heading. The aircraft completes the leg when it is at or above a given altitude, at no given position.
  • heading_to_dme_distance This value identifies a heading to a distance measuring equipment (DME) distance (VD). The aircraft flies a given heading to a given DME distance from a navigation aid.
  • heading_to_intercept This value identifies a heading to intercept the next leg (VI). The aircraft flies a given heading until it intercepts the next leg.
  • heading_to_manual_termination This value identifies a heading to a manual termination (VM). The aircraft flies a given heading until a manual termination by the pilot, usually to fly a radar vector.
  • heading_to_radial This value identifies a heading to a radial (VR). The aircraft flies a given heading to a given radial of a very high frequency omnidirectional range (VOR).
  • procedure_turn This value identifies a procedure turn (PI). From the fix of the leg, the aircraft flies an outbound leg. Then it makes a left turn or a right turn, and a turn of 180 degrees to intercept the next leg.
  • hold_to_altitude This value identifies a hold to an altitude (HA). The aircraft flies the holding pattern until it is at a given altitude.
  • hold_to_fix This value identifies a hold to a fix (HF). The aircraft flies one circuit of the holding pattern and completes the leg at the holding fix.
  • hold_to_manual_termination This value identifies a holding pattern to a manual termination (HM). The aircraft flies the holding pattern until a manual termination by the pilot.
missed_approachbooleanThe value is true when the leg is part of the missed approach procedure.
procedure_turnProcedureTurnThis field gives the type and the limits of the procedure turn of a procedure_turn leg. The field course of the leg is the outbound course, turn_direction is the direction of the first turn, and altitude is the procedure turn altitude. Other leg types shall not have this field.
recommended_navaidNavaidRefThis field gives the recommended navigation aid: the navigation aid that gives the course, the radial or the distance for the leg. A localizer can be the recommended navigation aid.
rhoLengthThis field gives the distance from the recommended navigation aid to the fix of the leg, as a length with its unit. On an arc_to_fix leg, it is the radius of the arc around the navigation aid. An arc_to_fix leg shall have this field. A leg with this field shall have recommended_navaid.
rnp_valueLength & anyThis field gives the lateral navigation accuracy that the leg needs, as a required navigation performance (RNP) value in nautical miles, as a length with its unit. It applies to this leg only, for example a leg of an RNP approach with authorization required. When the leg does not have this field, the value of the navigation specification applies.
speedSpeedConstraintThis field gives the speed constraint at the end of the leg.
thetaBearingThis field gives the bearing from the recommended navigation aid to the fix of the leg, as a bearing with its unit and reference. On a course_to_radial or heading_to_radial leg, it is the radial that ends the leg. A course_to_radial or heading_to_radial leg shall have this field. A leg with this field shall have recommended_navaid.
timeDurationThis field gives the published flight time of the leg, in minutes.
turn_directionenumThis field gives the direction of the turn onto this leg, as one of the enumerated values.
  • left The aircraft makes a left turn onto the leg.
  • right The aircraft makes a right turn onto the leg.
  • either The aircraft can make a left turn or a right turn onto the leg.
vertical_angle_degnumberThis field gives the vertical path angle to the fix, in degrees. A value less than zero is a descent.

LocalizerSelection

A localizer selection is a reference to one localizer of the resource catalogue, as a fix or as a recommended navigation aid.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies the localizer of this selection.
kind"localizer"yesThe value identifies this record as a localizer selection.

MinimaLine

A minima line is one line of the published minima of an approach: the minima for one type of guidance and one manoeuvre. It gives the minima for each aircraft approach category.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
category_minimalist of CategoryMinimumyesThis list contains the minima of the line for the aircraft approach categories. Each item gives the minima for one or more categories. A straight-in line with vertical guidance shall give decision altitudes, and other lines shall give minimum descent altitudes.
conditionstringThis field gives the condition in which this line applies, for example a remote altimeter setting or inoperative approach lights, as free text. A line without this field gives the standard minima.
height_referenceenumThis field gives the elevation from which the heights of the line are measured, as one of the enumerated values.
  • touchdown_zone This value identifies the highest elevation of the first 3000 feet of the landing surface, as for Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) heights above touchdown.
  • threshold This value identifies the elevation of the runway threshold, as for International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) decision heights.
  • aerodrome This value identifies the published elevation of the aerodrome, as for circling heights.
ils_categoryenumThis field gives the instrument landing system (ILS) category of the minima, as one of the enumerated values. Only a line of type ils or gls shall have this field.
  • I This value identifies category I minima with a decision height of 200 feet or more.
  • II This value identifies category II minima with a decision height from 100 feet to less than 200 feet.
  • III This value identifies category III minima with a decision height of less than 100 feet, or with no decision height.
labelstringThis field gives the name of the minima line as the chart shows it, for example S-ILS 31 or LNAV/VNAV.
lineenumyesThis field gives the guidance that the minima line uses, as one of the enumerated values.
  • ils This value identifies minima for an instrument landing system (ILS) approach, with a decision altitude.
  • gls This value identifies minima for a ground-based augmentation system landing system (GLS) approach, with a decision altitude.
  • par This value identifies minima for a precision approach radar (PAR) approach, with a decision altitude.
  • lpv This value identifies minima with localizer performance with vertical guidance (LPV) vertical guidance from satellite augmentation, with a decision altitude.
  • lnav_vnav This value identifies minima with lateral navigation (LNAV) and barometric or satellite vertical guidance, with a decision altitude.
  • rnp This value identifies minima of a required navigation performance (RNP) approach with authorization required, with a decision altitude for one RNP value.
  • lp This value identifies minima with localizer performance (LP) lateral guidance and no vertical guidance, with a minimum descent altitude (MDA).
  • lnav This value identifies minima with lateral navigation (LNAV) lateral guidance only, with a minimum descent altitude (MDA).
  • localizer This value identifies minima for a localizer approach without the glide slope, with a minimum descent altitude (MDA).
  • vor This value identifies minima for an approach with guidance from a very high frequency omnidirectional range (VOR) station, with a minimum descent altitude (MDA).
  • tacan This value identifies minima for an approach with guidance from a Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) station, with a minimum descent altitude (MDA).
  • ndb This value identifies minima for an approach with guidance from a non-directional beacon (NDB) station, with a minimum descent altitude (MDA).
  • asr This value identifies minima for an airport surveillance radar (ASR) approach, with a minimum descent altitude (MDA).
manoeuvreenumyesThis field gives the manoeuvre after the approach, as one of the enumerated values. A circling line shall not have runway, and other lines shall have it. The minima of a circling line shall be minimum descent altitudes, with the height above the aerodrome.
  • straight_in This value identifies a landing straight ahead on the runway of the final approach course.
  • circling This value identifies a visual manoeuvre around the aerodrome to land on a different runway or direction.
  • sidestep This value identifies a visual manoeuvre to land on a parallel runway next to the runway of the final approach.
remarkslist of stringThis list contains the remarks for this minima line, as free text.
rnp_valueLength & anyThis field gives the required navigation performance (RNP) value of the minima line, in nautical miles, as a length with its unit. An approach with authorization required can publish one line for each RNP value. Only a line of type rnp shall have this field.
runwayRunwayDesignatorThis field gives the designator of the runway of a straight-in line, or of the runway after a sidestep.

NavaidRadial

A navigation aid radial is a radial from a navigation aid, without a distance.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
navaidNavaidRefyesThis field gives the navigation aid that the radial is from.
radialBearingyesThis field gives the radial from the navigation aid, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

NavaidRef

A navigation aid reference is a navigation aid: its identifier and position, or a reference to a navigation aid or a localizer in the resource catalogue.

Type: object | ControlMeasureSelection | LocalizerSelection

NavigationSpecification

A navigation specification is the navigation that the procedure needs: conventional navigation, area navigation (RNAV) or required navigation performance (RNP). It gives the performance-based navigation (PBN) navigation specification, the RNP value, the sensors and the navigation aids.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
navigation_typeenumyesThis field gives the type of navigation of the procedure, as one of the enumerated values. A conventional procedure shall not have specification or rnp_value. An rnav or rnp procedure shall have a specification of its type.
  • conventional This value identifies navigation on courses and radials of ground navigation aids, without area navigation.
  • rnav This value identifies an area navigation (RNAV) navigation specification, without on-board performance monitoring and alerting.
  • rnp This value identifies a required navigation performance (RNP) navigation specification, with on-board performance monitoring and alerting.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about the navigation equipment of the procedure, as free text.
required_navaidslist of NavaidRefThis list contains the navigation aids that are necessary to fly the procedure. Each item is a navigation aid with its identifier and position, or a reference to a navigation aid in the resource catalogue.
rnp_valueLength & anyThis field gives the lateral navigation accuracy of the procedure, as a required navigation performance (RNP) value in nautical miles, as a length with its unit. An rnav procedure shall not have this field.
sensorslist of enumThis list contains the navigation sensors that the procedure needs. The aircraft uses one or more of them.
  • gnss
  • gbas
  • dme_dme
  • dme_dme_iru
  • vor_dme
  • vor
  • dme
  • tacan
  • ndb
  • ils
specificationenumThis field gives the performance-based navigation (PBN) navigation specification of the procedure, as one of the enumerated values.
  • rnav_10 This value identifies the RNAV 10 specification for oceanic and remote routes, with 10 nautical miles accuracy.
  • rnav_5 This value identifies the RNAV 5 specification for continental routes, with 5 nautical miles accuracy.
  • rnav_2 This value identifies the RNAV 2 specification for routes and terminal areas, with 2 nautical miles accuracy.
  • rnav_1 This value identifies the RNAV 1 specification for departures, arrivals and terminal areas, with 1 nautical mile accuracy.
  • rnp_4 This value identifies the RNP 4 specification for oceanic and remote routes, with 4 nautical miles accuracy.
  • rnp_2 This value identifies the RNP 2 specification for continental and remote routes, with 2 nautical miles accuracy.
  • rnp_1 This value identifies the RNP 1 specification for departures and arrivals, with 1 nautical mile accuracy.
  • advanced_rnp This value identifies the A-RNP specification for routes, terminal areas and approaches, with radius-to-fix legs.
  • rnp_apch This value identifies the RNP APCH specification for approaches with lateral navigation (LNAV), LNAV/VNAV, localizer performance (LP) or localizer performance with vertical guidance (LPV) minima.
  • rnp_ar_apch This value identifies the RNP AR APCH specification for approaches that need a special authorization.
  • rnp_0_3 This value identifies the RNP 0.3 specification for helicopter routes and terminal areas.

Obstacle

An obstacle is terrain or an object that the assessment of a segment uses.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
elevationElevationyesThis field gives the elevation of the top of the obstacle above mean sea level, as an elevation with its unit.
heightLengthThis field gives the height of the obstacle above the ground, as a length with its unit.
identstringThis field identifies this obstacle in its source data. An example is the number of the obstacle in an obstacle file.
obstacle_typeenumyesThis field gives the type of the obstacle, as one of the enumerated values.
  • terrain This value identifies the ground surface, for example a ridge or a peak.
  • structure This value identifies a building, a tower, an antenna or another object that people built.
  • vegetation This value identifies trees or other plants above the ground surface.
positionGeoPointThis field gives the geographic position of the obstacle, as latitude and longitude.

ObstacleAssessment

An obstacle clearance assessment is the result of an assessment of the terrain and the obstacles under the procedure. For each segment it gives the controlling obstacle, the obstacle clearance and the lowest altitude.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
assessed_atDateTimeThis field gives the time of the assessment.
criteriaenumyesThis field gives the design criteria of the assessment, as one of the enumerated values.
  • pans_ops This value identifies the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) criteria for the construction of instrument procedures in Doc 8168.
  • terps This value identifies the United States Standard for Terminal Instrument Procedures in Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Order 8260.3.
  • other This value identifies national or military criteria that criteria_document names.
criteria_documentstringThis field gives the document and the edition of the criteria, for example FAA Order 8260.3G.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about the assessment, as free text.
obstacle_datastringThis field gives the terrain data and obstacle data of the assessment, for example the name of the elevation model and its resolution, as free text.
segmentslist of SegmentAssessmentyesThis list contains the results of the assessment for the segments of the procedure.
toolToolThis field gives the software that made the assessment.

ProcedureTurn

A procedure turn is a course reversal from the outbound course onto the inbound course of an approach. The aircraft stays on the manoeuvring side of the outbound course and in the distance in remain_within.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
inbound_courseBearingThis field gives the course of the inbound leg after the course reversal, as a bearing with its unit and reference.
outbound_timeDurationThis field gives the flight time on the outbound leg before the aircraft turns back, in minutes. Base turns and some procedure turns publish this time.
remain_withinLengthThis field gives the distance from the fix of the leg in which the aircraft completes the procedure turn, as a length with its unit.
turn_typeenumyesThis field gives the type of the course reversal, as one of the enumerated values.
  • turn_45_180 This value identifies a 45 degree turn away from the outbound course, a straight leg, then a 180 degree turn back to the inbound course.
  • turn_80_260 This value identifies an 80 degree turn away from the outbound course and then a 260 degree turn the other way to the inbound course.
  • base_turn This value identifies a turn from an outbound course that diverges from the inbound course, as in a teardrop course reversal.

Provenance

A provenance is the origin of a navigation record: how its data were made, by which authority, for which aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle and with which tool.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
airac_cyclestringThis field gives the aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle of the data, as two digits of the year and two digits of the cycle, for example 2610.
authoritystringThis field gives the name of the authority that publishes the source data, for example FAA.
derivationenumyesThis field gives the way in which the data of the record were made, as one of the enumerated values.
  • published This value identifies data that an authority publishes, taken without changes.
  • derived This value identifies data that a tool converted or computed from published data.
  • synthesized This value identifies data that a tool designed where no published procedure or record exists.
  • authored This value identifies data that a person wrote for a mission or a scenario.
effective_fromDateTimeThis field gives the time of the start of the period in which the data are effective.
effective_untilDateTimeThis field gives the time of the end of the period in which the data are effective.
generated_atDateTimeThis field gives the time of the conversion or the generation of the data.
publicationDocumentRefThis field identifies the publication from which the data come. An example is the chart of the procedure.
toolToolThis field gives the software tool that converted or made the data.

RadarApproach

A radar approach is the final approach of a precision approach radar (PAR) or an airport surveillance radar (ASR) approach, which a controller gives from the radar. The field approach_type of the procedure gives the type of radar.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
coverageRadarCoverageThis field gives the volume in which the radar gives the approach.
final_approach_courseBearingyesThis field gives the final approach course of the radar approach, as a bearing with its unit and reference.
glide_path_angle_degnumberThis field gives the angle between the precision approach radar (PAR) glide path and a horizontal line, in degrees. A PAR approach shall have this field, and an airport surveillance radar (ASR) approach shall not have it.
lost_communicationslist of stringThis list contains the lost communications instructions for the radar approach, as free text.
missed_approach_point_distanceLengthThis field gives the distance of the missed approach point of an airport surveillance radar (ASR) approach from the runway threshold, as a length with its unit. A precision approach radar (PAR) approach shall not have this field.
positionGeoPointThis field gives the geographic position of the radar antenna, as latitude and longitude.
recommended_altitudeslist of RecommendedAltitudeThis list contains the altitudes that the controller recommends at distances from the runway on an airport surveillance radar (ASR) approach. A precision approach radar (PAR) approach shall not have this field.
runwayRunwayDesignatoryesThis field gives the designator of the runway of the radar approach.
