threshold_crossing_heightLengthThis field gives the threshold crossing height (TCH) of the precision approach radar (PAR) glide path, as a length with its unit. It is the height of the glide path above the landing threshold.

RadarCoverage

A radar coverage is the volume of the radar on the final approach. The azimuth limits are angles from the final approach course, and the elevation limits are angles above a horizontal line.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
azimuth_left_degnumberThis field gives the azimuth limit left of the final approach course, in degrees.
azimuth_right_degnumberThis field gives the azimuth limit right of the final approach course, in degrees.
elevation_lower_degnumberThis field gives the lower elevation limit of the precision approach radar (PAR), in degrees. A value less than zero is below the horizontal. An airport surveillance radar (ASR) approach shall not have this field.
elevation_upper_degnumberThis field gives the upper elevation limit of the precision approach radar (PAR), in degrees. An airport surveillance radar (ASR) approach shall not have this field.
rangeLengthyesThis field gives the range of the radar coverage on the final approach, from the runway threshold, as a length with its unit.

RadialDme

A radial and distance definition is a fix defined by a navigation aid, a radial from it and a distance from it. An example is the fix LSV 040/12, at 12 nautical miles on the 040 degree radial of the navigation aid LSV.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
additional_radialslist of NavaidRadialThis field gives the other radials that also define the fix, each with its navigation aid. The fix is at the intersection of these radials with the first radial.
distanceLengthyesThis field gives the distance from the navigation aid to the fix, as a length with its unit.
navaidNavaidRefyesThis field gives the navigation aid that the radial and the distance are measured from.
radialBearingyesThis field gives the radial from the navigation aid to the fix, as a bearing with its unit and reference.

RecommendedAltitude

A recommended altitude is an altitude that the controller recommends at one distance from the runway on an airport surveillance radar (ASR) approach.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
altitudeAltitude & anyyesThis field gives the recommended altitude above mean sea level at this distance, as an altitude with its unit and reference.
distanceLengthyesThis field gives the distance from the runway threshold, as a length with its unit.

Remarks

Type: list of string

SegmentAssessment

A segment assessment is the obstacle clearance result for one segment of the procedure.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
controlling_obstacleObstacleThis field gives the controlling obstacle: the obstacle that sets the lowest altitude of the segment.
from_fixstringThis field gives the identifier of the fix at the start of the segment.
minimum_altitudeAltitude & anyyesThis field gives the lowest altitude of the segment above mean sea level that keeps the obstacle clearance, as an altitude with its unit and reference.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about the result for the segment, as free text.
obstacle_clearanceLengthyesThis field gives the obstacle clearance that the assessment applies above the controlling obstacle, as a length with its unit. It is the minimum obstacle clearance of International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Doc 8168 or the required obstacle clearance of Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Order 8260.3.
satisfiedbooleanThe value is true when the published altitudes of the segment are at or above minimum_altitude. The value is false when a published altitude of the segment is below minimum_altitude.
segmentenumyesThis field gives the type of the segment, as one of the enumerated values.
  • departure This value identifies the climb from the runway along a departure route.
  • arrival This value identifies the route from the en-route structure to the start of the approach.
  • feeder This value identifies a route from the en-route structure to the initial approach fix.
  • initial This value identifies the initial approach segment, from the initial approach fix to the intermediate fix.
  • intermediate This value identifies the intermediate approach segment, from the intermediate fix to the final approach fix.
  • final This value identifies the final approach segment, from the final approach fix to the runway or the missed approach point.
  • missed_approach This value identifies the climb from the missed approach point to the holding fix or the en-route structure.
  • circling This value identifies the visual manoeuvring area around the aerodrome for a circling approach.
  • holding This value identifies the protected area of a holding pattern of the procedure.
to_fixstringThis field gives the identifier of the fix at the end of the segment.
transitionstringThis field gives the identifier of the transition of the segment, as in ident of the transition.

SpeedConstraint

A speed constraint is a speed restriction with its type and its speed.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
kindenumyesThis field gives the type of the speed restriction, as one of the enumerated values.
  • at The aircraft flies at the speed in value.
  • at_or_below The speed is a maximum speed. The aircraft flies at or below the speed in value.
  • at_or_above The speed is a minimum speed. The aircraft flies at or above the speed in value.
valueSpeedyesThis field gives the speed of the restriction, as a speed with its unit.

TakeoffMinimum

A takeoff minimum is the lowest weather for a takeoff on this departure. It shall have visibility or runway_visual_range.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
ceilingLengthThis field gives the lowest ceiling for the takeoff, above the aerodrome, as a length with its unit.
climb_gradientClimbGradientThis field gives the climb gradient that the aircraft needs to use these minima.
conditionstringThis field gives the condition in which this takeoff minimum applies, for example the number of engines, as free text.
remarkslist of stringThis list contains the remarks for the takeoff, for example obstacle notes, as free text.
runwayRunwayDesignatorThis field gives the designator of the runway of the takeoff minimum.
runway_visual_rangeLength & anyThis field gives the lowest runway visual range (RVR) for the takeoff, as a length with its unit. The unit is feet or metres.
visibilityVisibilityThis field gives the lowest visibility for the takeoff.

Tool

A tool is a software tool with its version.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
namestringyesThis field gives the name of the software tool.
versionstringThis field gives the version of the software tool.

Transition

A transition is one transition or route segment of a procedure.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
identstringThis field identifies this transition. Examples are the entry fix and the runway. The common route and the final approach do not have this field.
legslist of LegyesThis list contains the legs of the transition, in the sequence of flight, in order.
transition_typeenumThis field gives the role of the transition in the procedure, as one of the enumerated values. A runway transition joins the runway to the common route, and an en route transition joins the common route to the enroute structure. An approach transition joins the enroute structure to the final approach, and the final approach is the segment from the final approach course to the missed approach point.
  • runway_transition
  • common_route
  • enroute_transition
  • approach_transition
  • final_approach

Visibility

A visibility is a horizontal visibility with its unit.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
unitenumyesThis field gives the unit of the visibility, as one of the enumerated values.
  • m This value identifies a visibility in metres.
  • km This value identifies a visibility in kilometres.
  • sm This value identifies a visibility in statute miles, as United States charts publish it.
valuenumberyesThis field gives the value of the visibility, in the unit of unit.

Runway

urn:openaix:schema:runway:0.2.0-draft.1

runway

A runway is one runway with its two ends, its dimensions and its surface. Each end has the threshold, the heading and the equipment that is necessary for a flight simulator.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
airfieldIdentifierThis field identifies the airfield that has this runway. In the runway list of an airfield, the value shall be the identifier of that airfield.
designatorstringyesThis field gives the designator of the runway, for example 03L/21R. The value shall contain the designators of the two runway ends, with / between them.
endslist of RunwayEndyesThis list contains the two ends of the runway. The two ends shall have opposite designators. Each runway end in the airfield has a different designator.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this runway. Other resources and orders use this stable identifier to refer to this runway.
kind"runway"yesThe value identifies this record as a runway record. The value selects this navigation contract.
lengthLengthyesThis field gives the published length of the runway, as a length with its unit.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this runway, for display.
provenanceProvenanceThis field gives the provenance of this runway as structured data: how the data were made, the authority, the aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle and the tool that made them.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this runway. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
sourcestringThis field gives the source of this record. The value gives the authority that publishes the data, and the cycle, for example FAA CIFP cycle 2610. A record that an author writes does not have this field. The field provenance gives the same facts as structured data.
surfaceenumThis field gives the surface of the runway, as one of the enumerated values.
  • hard This value identifies a surface of asphalt, concrete or an equivalent hard material.
  • soft This value identifies a surface of gravel, grass or ground, without asphalt or concrete.
  • water This value identifies an area of water that seaplanes use as a runway.
widthLengthThis field gives the published width of the runway, as a length with its unit.

ArrestingGear

An arresting gear is one cable or barrier across the runway that stops aircraft.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
distance_from_thresholdLengthyesThis field gives the distance from the landing threshold of this end to the cable, as a length with its unit.
typeenumyesThis field gives the type of the arresting gear, as one of the enumerated values.
  • BAK_12 This value identifies the BAK-12 arresting gear with a cable.
  • BAK_13 This value identifies the BAK-13 arresting gear with a cable.
  • BAK_14 This value identifies the BAK-14 arresting gear with a cable that retracts.
  • BAK_15 This value identifies the BAK-15 barrier with a net.
  • MA_1A This value identifies the MA-1A barrier with a net and a cable.
  • E_5 This value identifies the E-5 arresting gear with a chain.
  • E_28 This value identifies the E-28 arresting gear with a cable.

Lighting

Runway lighting is the approach lights, the runway lights and the visual slope indicator.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
approach_lightingenumThis field gives the approach lighting system, as one of the enumerated values.
  • ALSF_1 This value identifies ALSF-1: a high intensity approach lighting system with sequenced flashing lights, for Category I approaches.
  • ALSF_2 This value identifies ALSF-2: a high intensity approach lighting system with sequenced flashing lights, for Category II and III approaches.
  • MALSR This value identifies MALSR: a medium intensity approach lighting system with runway alignment indicator lights.
  • MALSF This value identifies MALSF: a medium intensity approach lighting system with sequenced flashing lights.
  • MALS This value identifies MALS: a medium intensity approach lighting system.
  • SSALR This value identifies SSALR: a simplified short approach lighting system with runway alignment indicator lights.
  • SSALF This value identifies SSALF: a simplified short approach lighting system with sequenced flashing lights.
  • SSALS This value identifies SSALS: a simplified short approach lighting system.
  • ODALS This value identifies ODALS: an omnidirectional approach lighting system.
edge_lightsbooleanThe value is true when the runway has edge lights. The value is false when the runway has no edge lights.
reilbooleanThe value is true when the runway end has runway end identifier lights (REIL). The value is false when the runway end has no REIL.
slope_indicatorenumThis field gives the visual slope indicator for the approach, as one of the enumerated values.
  • PAPI This value identifies the precision approach path indicator (PAPI). It is one row of light units that show the aircraft position in relation to the approach path.
  • VASI This value identifies the visual approach slope indicator (VASI). It is two or three rows of light units that show the aircraft position in relation to the approach path.

RunwayEnd

A runway end is one end of a runway and the landing direction to that end. It has the threshold, the heading, the approach equipment and the local pattern values.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
arresting_gearlist of ArrestingGearThis list contains the arresting gear across the runway. Distances are from the threshold of this end.
designatorRunwayDesignatoryesThis field gives the designator of this runway end. It is the magnetic heading in degrees divided by 10, with an optional suffix L, R, C, W, S, G or U.
displaced_thresholdLengthThis field gives the distance from the runway end to the displaced threshold, as a length with its unit. The record does not have this field when the landing threshold is at the runway end.
headingBearingyesThis field gives the bearing of the runway in this landing direction, as a bearing with its unit and reference. A magnetic heading includes the declination of the airfield. Thus, a consumer can calculate the true heading from it.
lightingLightingThis field gives the runway lighting for this landing direction.
localizerIdentifierThis field identifies the localizer that is for this runway end. The field runway of the localizer shall identify this runway end.
thresholdGeoPointyesThis field gives the geographic position of the landing threshold for this landing direction, as latitude and longitude.
threshold_crossing_heightLengthThis field gives the threshold crossing height (TCH) of the approach path, as a length with its unit. It is the height of the approach path above the landing threshold.
threshold_elevationElevationThis field gives the elevation of the landing threshold above mean sea level, as an elevation with its unit.
traffic_patternTrafficPatternThis field gives the traffic pattern values for this landing direction. They replace the values of the airfield pattern, and each value is optional.

Standard conventional load

urn:openaix:schema:scl:0.2.0-draft.1

scl

A standard conventional load (SCL) is one store configuration of one aircraft type. It gives the stores of each aircraft, their stations and fuzes, the gun rounds and the countermeasures. The load does not show that it is possible to install the stores on the aircraft.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastring (uri)This field identifies the schema that validates this document.
aircraft_typeIdentifieryesThis field identifies the aircraft type that this load is for. Each flight with this standard conventional load (SCL) shall have this aircraft type.
codestringThis field gives the standard conventional load (SCL) code of the load, such as 4G12.3A.1X.2. Some units use these short codes. They are not a standard for all units. OpenAIX does not use the code to find the stores. The stores and the stations of the record are the reference.
countermeasuresCountermeasuresThis field gives the chaff, the flares and the countermeasure program of the load.
erastringThis field gives the era of the load, such as modern or retro, as free text. The unit sets its eras.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
gun_roundsintegerThis field gives the number of gun rounds in each aircraft.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this standard conventional load (SCL). Other records and orders use it to refer to this SCL.
kind"scl"yesThe value identifies this record as a standard conventional load (SCL).
laser_codeLaserCodeThis field gives the default laser code for the weapons of this load. A store entry can give a different code.
missionslist of SCLMissionThis list contains the tasking families and roles that this load is applicable to. The list shall include the tasking of each flight that has this load as its primary load.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this standard conventional load (SCL), for display. An example is AI-1 GBU-12.
remarksstringThis field gives the remarks about the load, as free text.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the external resource catalogue that resolves the references of this record. The reference identifies the catalogue and gives its revision.
scl_numberstringThis field gives the number of the load in the table of the unit, such as DTA05 or 101, as free text.
sourceDocumentRefThis field identifies the source document. The reference identifies the document. It may also give a revision and a locator.
stationslist of StationLoadThis list contains the weapon stations of the load, with the stores on each station.
storeslist of StoreLoadThis list contains the stores of the load, with the quantity of each store in each aircraft. This list does not give the stations. Each store shall occur one time in the list. With stations, the quantity of each store shall be equal to the sum on its stations.
variant_tagslist of stringThis list contains the labels of this load variant, such as 120B or Pre-2015. Each label shows a difference from the other load variants with the same number.

Countermeasures

A countermeasure load is the chaff, the flares and the dispenser program of a load.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
chaffintegerThis field gives the number of chaff cartridges in each aircraft.
flaresintegerThis field gives the number of flares in each aircraft.
programstringThis field gives the countermeasure program of the dispensers, as free text.

Fuze

A fuze setting is the fuzes of a weapon, their function and their time adjustments. The extensions.sim.dcs data of a station keeps the Digital Combat Simulator (DCS) values of the fuze.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
arming_delay_snumberThis field gives the time after the aircraft releases the weapon until the fuze can operate, in seconds.
delay_msnumberThis field gives the time after the weapon hits the target until the fuze functions, in milliseconds.
functionenumyesThis field gives the function of the fuze, as one of the enumerated values.
  • instantaneous
  • delay
  • proximity
  • airburst
height_of_burstLengthThis field gives the height above the ground at which the fuze functions, as a length with its unit.
nose_fuzestringThis field gives the nose fuze of the weapon, such as DSU-33, as free text.
tail_fuzestringThis field gives the tail fuze of the weapon, such as FMU-139, as free text.

SCLMission

A standard conventional load (SCL) mission is a tasking family and a role for which the load is applicable.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
roleenumThis field gives the role or mission type in the tasking family, as one of the enumerated values. It agrees with the role field or the mission_type field of the tasking. If the entry does not give a role, the load is applicable to all roles of the tasking family. The role shall be a role of the tasking family.
  • aeromedical_evacuation
  • air_assault
  • air_interdiction
  • airdrop
  • airlift
  • combat_search_and_rescue
  • dead
  • fac_a
  • fighter_sweep
  • humanitarian_assistance
  • interception
  • maritime_attack
  • noncombatant_evacuation
  • scar
  • scheduled_cas
  • sead
  • search_and_rescue
  • strike
taskingenumyesThis field gives the tasking family, as the kind field of an air tasking order (ATO) tasking gives it, as one of the enumerated values.
  • preplanned_attack
  • on_call_cas
  • cap
  • escort
  • refueling
  • airborne_control
  • reconnaissance
  • electromagnetic
  • transport
  • personnel_recovery
  • training
  • custom
  • counterair
  • counterland_control

StationLoad

A station load is the stores on one weapon station of the aircraft.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
itemslist of StoreLoadyesThis list contains the stores on this station.
rackIdentifierThis field identifies the store of the rack type that has the other stores on this station.
stationstringyesThis field gives the label of the weapon station in the flight manual or the simulator, such as 3 or 5L, as free text. Each station shall occur one time in the list of stations.

StoreLoad

A store load is one store of a load with its quantity, fuze, laser code and program.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
fuzeFuzeThis field gives the fuze setting of the store.
laser_codeLaserCodeThis field gives the laser code of the store. It replaces the laser code of the standard conventional load (SCL) for this store.
programstringThis field gives the weapon program of the store, as free text.
quantityintegeryesThis field gives the number of items of the store in each aircraft, or on the station in a station entry.
storeIdentifieryesThis field identifies the store that this entry is for.

Territory

urn:openaix:schema:territory:0.2.0-draft.1

territory

A territory is a land area with an affiliation: friendly, hostile or neutral. The required shape gives the boundary, and it has priority over the country codes. Thus a territory can be in a real, a historic or a fictional world. Without vertical limits, a territory runs from the surface with no upper limit.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
activeActivationThis field gives the time interval during which this territory is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.
affiliationenumyesThis field gives the affiliation of the territory, as one of the enumerated values. The values are the standard identities friend, hostile and neutral of MIL-STD-2525 and APP-6.
  • friend This value identifies land that friendly forces hold or that is friendly to them.
  • hostile This value identifies land that enemy forces hold or that is hostile.
  • neutral This value identifies land that is neither friendly nor hostile, for example a neutral country.
countrieslist of stringThis list contains the country codes of the territory, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes such as SYR. The codes are labels for maps of the real world. The geometry gives the boundary.
descriptionstringThis field gives the information about this territory and its local conditions, as free text.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
geometryGeometry_polygon | Geometry_rectangle | Geometry_ellipse | Geometry_geojson_polygonyesThis field gives the horizontal geometry of the territory: a polygon or a GeoJSON polygon or multipolygon (RFC 7946).
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this territory. Other records and orders use it to refer to this territory.
lower_limitVerticalLimitThis field gives the floor of the territory: an altitude with its reference, or the surface. This field is optional; without it, the floor is the surface.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this territory, for display.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about this territory, as free text.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this territory. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
type"TERRITORY"yesThe value identifies this record as a territory. The value is the same for all territories.
upper_limitVerticalLimitThis field gives the ceiling of the territory: an altitude with its reference, or no limit. This field is optional; without it, the territory has no upper limit.

Time-Sensitive Targets (TST)

urn:openaix:schema:tst:0.2.0-draft.1

tst

Time-sensitive targets (TST) are targets that it is necessary to engage immediately. A target is on the list when it is dangerous to friendly forces at this time or in a short time. A target of opportunity that is very important and available for a short time only is also on the list. Each entry has the data to find, identify and engage the target in its window.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastring (uri)This field identifies the schema that validates this document.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
kind"tst"yesThe value identifies this record as a time-sensitive target (TST) list.
metaMetadataThis field gives the identification, revision and issue data of this list.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the external resource catalogue that resolves the references of the list. The reference identifies the catalogue and gives its revision.
schema_version"0.2.0-draft.1"This field gives the version of the openAIX schema that this time-sensitive target (TST) list agrees with.
targetslist of TSTEntryyesThis list contains the time-sensitive targets of the mission. It is necessary to engage each target immediately.

EngagementMeans

An approved weapon system is a weapon system or an aircraft type that has clearance to engage the target, with its weapon.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
sclIdentifierThis field identifies the standard conventional load (SCL) that is the load of the aircraft.
storeIdentifierThis field identifies the store that is the weapon. When the entry gives a standard conventional load (SCL), the SCL shall contain the store.
systemstringyesThis field gives the weapon system or type of aircraft, such as F-15E, M777 or HIMARS, as free text.

TSTEntry

A time-sensitive target entry is one row on the time-sensitive target (TST) list. The joint force commander designates each TST and has its engagement authority. The joint force commander may delegate this authority to a component commander or to a lower level. Forces prosecute a TST with dynamic targeting: find, fix, track, target, engage and assess.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
activity_windowWindowThis field gives the time interval during which the target is possibly there or active.
authorized_engagement_meanslist of EngagementMeansThis list contains the weapon systems that have clearance to prosecute the time-sensitive target (TST). Each entry gives the system, and can refer to the standard conventional load (SCL) and the weapon in the resource catalogue.
categorystringThis field gives the type of the target, such as air defence or leadership, as free text. The types are local values and not a code list of the joint force.
engagement_authorityIdentifierThis field identifies the command and control agency that gives approval for the engagement of this target. The joint force commander has this authority and may delegate it to a component commander or to a lower level.
expected_locationslist of objectThis list contains the positions at which the target can possibly be.
expiration_criteriastringThis field gives the conditions or time for the removal of the target from the list, as free text.
expires_atDateTimeThis field gives the time at which the target goes off the list, if no other condition removes it first.
priorityintegerThis field gives the priority of this target in relation to the other time-sensitive targets in the list. Priority 1 is the highest. The value is a local priority and not a priority level from the doctrine of the joint force.
roe_constraintsstringThis field gives the rules of engagement (ROE) limits for this time-sensitive target (TST), as free text. These limits add to the usual ROE.
targetIdentifierThis field identifies the target that is this entry, in the resource catalogue.
target_descriptionstringThis field gives the data about the type of the target and the signs that units can see, as free text.
tst_numberstringyesThis field identifies this time-sensitive target (TST). Examples are TST-01 and TST-02.

Airspace coordination area

urn:openaix:schema:measure-aca:0.2.0-draft.1

measure-aca

An airspace coordination area (ACA) is a block or corridor of airspace above a target area. In it, friendly aircraft are reasonably safe from friendly surface fires. The airspace control authority establishes a formal airspace coordination area on the request of a component. It has a minimum altitude, a maximum altitude, a baseline, a width on each side of the baseline and effective times. In an informal airspace coordination area, time, lateral distance or altitude keeps aircraft and surface fires apart. A battalion or higher headquarters gives approval for it.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
aca_kindenumyesThis field gives the type of airspace coordination area (ACA): formal or informal, as one of the enumerated values. In openAIX, an ACA of the type formal is a volume, and an ACA of the type informal gives only its method of separation. The airspace control authority makes an ACA of the type formal when a component sends a request for it. It has altitudes, a baseline, a width and the times when it is active. In an ACA of the type informal, time, lateral distance or altitude gives the separation between aircraft and surface fires. A battalion or a higher unit gives the approval for an ACA of the type informal.
  • formal The airspace control authority makes the airspace coordination area (ACA) when a component sends a request for it. It has a minimum and a maximum altitude, a baseline, a width and the times when it is active (JP 3-09, Appendix A, 5.d).
  • informal Time, lateral distance or altitude gives the separation between aircraft and surface fires. A battalion or a higher unit gives the approval for it (JP 3-09, Appendix A, 5.d).
activeActivationyesThis field gives the time interval during which this airspace coordination area is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.
channelslist of IdentifierThis list identifies the communications channels of this airspace coordination area.
componentslist of AirspaceComponentThis list contains the airspace components of the coordination volume. A formal airspace coordination area (ACA) is usually a corridor component along its baseline, between the minimum and maximum altitudes.
controlling_agencyIdentifierThis field identifies the agency that controls the operations in this airspace coordination area.
coordination_instructionslist of stringThis list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this airspace coordination area has an effect on.
descriptionstringThis field gives the information about this airspace coordination area and its local conditions, as free text.
establishing_authorityIdentifierThis field identifies the authority that set this airspace coordination area.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this airspace coordination area. Other records and orders use it to refer to this airspace coordination area.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this airspace coordination area, for display.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about this airspace coordination area, as free text.
purposestringThis field gives the task or objective of this airspace coordination area, as free text.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this airspace coordination area. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
restrictionslist of stringThis list contains the conditions that control the operations in this airspace coordination area.
separationenumThis field gives the method of separation between aircraft and surface fires in an informal airspace coordination area (ACA), as one of the enumerated values.
  • time Aircraft and surface fires use the area at different times.
  • lateral Lateral distance gives the separation between aircraft and surface fires.
  • altitude Altitude gives the separation between aircraft and surface fires.
  • combined This value identifies separation by time, lateral distance and altitude together.
type"ACA"yesThe value identifies this record as an airspace coordination area. The value selects the data contract of the control measure.

Area of responsibility

urn:openaix:schema:measure-aor:0.2.0-draft.1

measure-aor

An area of responsibility (AOR) is the geographic area of a commander, in which that commander has the authority to plan and conduct operations. The airspace control area (ACAR) can be the same as the AOR of a regional commander. It can be the same as the joint operations area of the commander of the joint force command. The ACAR can also be smaller than the AOR, because of limits of nations or of International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), or larger. The responsible_agency and gates fields are openAIX planning fields.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
activeActivationyesThis field gives the time interval during which this area of responsibility is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.
descriptionstringThis field gives the information about this area of responsibility and its local conditions, as free text.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
gateslist of IdentifierThis list identifies the entry and exit gates of this area.
geometryGeometry_polygon | Geometry_circle | Geometry_rectangle | Geometry_ellipse | Geometry_geojson_polygonyesThis field gives the horizontal geometry of the area of responsibility: a polygon, a circle, a rectangle, an ellipse or a GeoJSON polygon.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this area of responsibility. Other records and orders use it to refer to this area of responsibility.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this area of responsibility, for display.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about this area of responsibility, as free text.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this area of responsibility. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
responsible_agencyIdentifierThis field identifies the agency that controls this area.
type"AOR"yesThe value identifies this record as an area of responsibility. The value selects the data contract of the control measure.

Fire support or manoeuvre area

urn:openaix:schema:measure-area:0.2.0-draft.1

measure-area

A surface fire support or manoeuvre area is an area on the ground in two dimensions, with no vertical limits. The code NFA prevents fires and their effects, and with the code FFA, fires can occur without more coordination. With the code RFA, fires that do not obey the restrictions of the area can occur only with coordination. The code EA identifies the engagement area that the commander plans, and AOA identifies the amphibious objective area. The codes OBJ, BP, AA, NAI and TAI identify ground manoeuvre graphics. The code FSA identifies a sea area for fire support ships.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
activeActivationyesThis field gives the time interval during which this area is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.
coordination_instructionslist of stringThis list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this area has an effect on.
descriptionstringThis field gives the information about this area and its local conditions, as free text.
establishing_authorityIdentifierThis field identifies the headquarters that set the area.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
geometryGeometry_polygon | Geometry_circle | Geometry_polyarc | Geometry_rectangle | Geometry_ellipse | Geometry_geojson_polygonyesThis field gives the horizontal geometry of the area on the ground or at sea: a polygon, or a radius from a centre point. A geojson geometry (RFC 7946) of the same shape is also correct. The boundary follows terrain features that are easy to identify.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this area. Other records and orders use it to refer to this area.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this area, for display.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about this area, as free text.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this area. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
restrictionslist of stringThis list contains the restrictions on fires or tasks. A restrictive fire area (RFA) shall give them.
typeenumyesThis field gives the catalogue code of this control measure, as one of the enumerated values. The code identifies the definition of the control measure in doctrine. The catalogue of control measures gives its class and the source of its definition.
  • AOA An amphibious objective area (AOA) is a geographical area that the initiating directive gives for command and control. It contains the objectives that the amphibious task force is to make safe.
  • EA An engagement area (EA) is an area of ground manoeuvre control in which the commander plans to contain and destroy an enemy force. The commander uses the massed effects of all available weapons and the systems that help them. Close air support is an example. The commander may divide the area into smaller areas for subordinate units.
  • NFA A no-fire area (NFA) is a restrictive area that prohibits joint fires and their effects into the area. The establishing headquarters (HQ) may give approval for fires into it, one mission at a time. When an enemy force in the area engages a friendly force, the friendly force may use minimal force in self-defence. A unit of any size may establish an NFA.
  • RFA A restrictive fire area (RFA) is an area with special restrictions on joint fires. Units do not fire joint fires that are more than these restrictions, or that have such effects, without coordination with the establishing headquarters (HQ). A manoeuvre battalion or higher usually establishes it. Restrictive fire areas can also be on-call areas that units prepare before the operation.
  • FFA A free-fire area (FFA) is a permissive area for fires. Any weapon system may fire into it without further coordination with the establishing headquarters (HQ). Joint fires can occur more quickly in it, and it helps aircraft jettison munitions. Only the commander with jurisdiction, usually at division or higher, may establish it.
  • OBJ An objective (OBJ) is a location for the orientation of operations, the phases of operations, changes of direction and unity of effort. It can be a terrain objective or a force objective.
  • BP A battle position (BP) is a defence location in the direction of a likely enemy avenue of approach. It is not an area of operations.
  • AA An assembly area (AA) is an area where a unit makes its preparation for an operation.
  • NAI A named area of interest (NAI) is a geospatial area, or a systems node or link, where forces get information for a specified information requirement. This information usually shows enemy and adversary courses of action.
  • TAI A target area of interest (TAI) is a geographical area where friendly forces find and engage high-value targets.
  • FSA A fire support area (FSA) is a sea manoeuvre area that the naval force commander gives to fire support ships. From this area, the ships supply gunfire support to an amphibious operation. The officer in tactical command establishes it.
  • AXIS An axis of advance is the general area through which the bulk of the combat power of a unit must move. A commander uses it to make the force bypass locations that could delay it. It also shows that the force does not have to clear all of the assigned area. It shows a unit in an encirclement, exploitation or pursuit that it must move quickly toward an objective. Bypass criteria go with it. Any manoeuvre echelon can use one. The axis of a subordinate unit stays inside the axis of its higher headquarters.
  • CFZ A critical friendly zone is an area of friendly weapons locating radar coverage that a commander designates. It is critical to the protection of an asset. The loss of that asset would seriously jeopardize the mission. The zone needs weapons locating radar coverage and attack assets that can give counterfire. The supporting field artillery unit puts enemy indirect fire that the radar acquires into the zone ahead of all other counterfire targets.

Coordination level or coordinating altitude

urn:openaix:schema:measure-cl:0.2.0-draft.1

measure-cl

A coordination level or coordinating altitude is one altitude or height that divides airspace users. The code CL is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) coordination level, and the code CA is the coordinating altitude of JP 3-52. The record can identify the agencies that control the airspace below and above the level. The lateral limits come from text or from unit boundaries, not from this record.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
activeActivationyesThis field gives the time interval during which this coordination level or coordinating altitude is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.
coordination_instructionslist of stringThis list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this coordination level or coordinating altitude has an effect on.
descriptionstringThis field gives the information about this coordination level or coordinating altitude and its local conditions, as free text.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
geometryGeometry_vertical & anyyesThis field gives the vertical geometry of the coordination level: one altitude or height.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this coordination level or coordinating altitude. Other records and orders use it to refer to this coordination level or coordinating altitude.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this coordination level or coordinating altitude, for display.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about this coordination level or coordinating altitude, as free text.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this coordination level or coordinating altitude. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
responsibility_aboveIdentifierThis field identifies the agency that controls the airspace above the level.
responsibility_belowIdentifierThis field identifies the agency that controls the airspace below the level.
typeenumyesThis field gives the catalogue code of this control measure, as one of the enumerated values. The code identifies the definition of the control measure in doctrine. The catalogue of control measures gives its class and the source of its definition.
  • CL A coordination level (CL) is one altitude or height that sets airspace control responsibilities. The CL deconflicts airspace users, and this is its primary function. It usually divides the users above it from the users below it.
  • CA A coordinating altitude (CA) is an airspace coordinating measure that uses altitude to separate users and as the transition between different airspace control elements. Airspace users should coordinate with these elements before they fly or fire through it.

Fire support line

urn:openaix:schema:measure-fire-support-line:0.2.0-draft.1

measure-fire-support-line

A fire support line is one of four lines for the coordination of fires. The headquarters of a ground force, of an amphibious force or of the two forces together sets it. On the far side of a coordinated fire line (CFL), in the boundaries of its headquarters, standard indirect fires can occur without more coordination. Other forces should coordinate their fires on the far side of a fire support coordination line (FSCL) with its commander. A restrictive fire line (RFL) between friendly forces that come together prevents fires and their effects across it without coordination. Between a battlefield coordination line (BCL) and the FSCL, Marine aircraft can attack surface targets without approval from the ground combat element (GCE) commander.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
activeActivationyesThis field gives the time interval during which this fire support line is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.
coordination_instructionslist of stringThis list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this fire support line has an effect on.
descriptionstringThis field gives the information about this fire support line and its local conditions, as free text.
establishing_authorityIdentifierThis field identifies the headquarters that set the line.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
geometryGeometry_line | Geometry_geojson_lineyesThis field gives the horizontal geometry of the line: geographic positions in sequence. A geojson geometry (RFC 7946) of the same shape is also correct.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this fire support line. Other records and orders use it to refer to this fire support line.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this fire support line, for display.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about this fire support line, as free text.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this fire support line. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
typeenumyesThis field gives the catalogue code of this control measure, as one of the enumerated values. The code identifies the definition of the control measure in doctrine. The catalogue of control measures gives its class and the source of its definition.
  • FSCL A fire support coordination line (FSCL) is a line in the area of operations (AO) for the coordination of fires by other force elements. A land or amphibious force commander establishes it. These fires can have an effect on the current and planned operations of that commander. Other force elements should coordinate these fires with that commander. The establishing commander should coordinate the line with the affected commanders.
  • CFL A coordinated fire line (CFL) is a line that a land headquarters sets. Beyond this line, conventional indirect surface fire support means may fire at any time without further coordination. This is applicable only in the boundaries of the establishing headquarters.
  • RFL A restrictive fire line (RFL) is a line between converging friendly forces, of which one or both may move. It prohibits joint fires and the effects of joint fires across the line without coordination with the affected force. Its function is to prevent friendly fire and the duplication of engagements by the converging forces. The commander common to the converging forces establishes it.
  • BCL A battlefield coordination line (BCL) is a fire support coordination measure of the Marine Corps. Between it and the fire support coordination line (FSCL), Marine air-ground task force (MAGTF) aviation quickly attacks surface targets of opportunity. The approval of the ground combat element (GCE) commander of the area where the targets are is not necessary. The MAGTF commander establishes the BCL. An airspace coordination area (ACA) or a kill box usually includes the area between the BCL and the FSCL.

Identification safety range

urn:openaix:schema:measure-isr:0.2.0-draft.1

measure-isr

An identification safety range (ISR) is the minimum range to which aircraft can close to a maritime force without positive identification. This identification shows that the aircraft are friendly. This range makes sure that the maritime force does not mistake the aircraft for hostile. The officer in tactical command sets it. The range moves with the maritime force. A record can give a circle geometry for display at a specified time.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
activeActivationyesThis field gives the time interval during which this identification safety range is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.
coordination_instructionslist of stringThis list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this identification safety range has an effect on.
descriptionstringThis field gives the information about this identification safety range and its local conditions, as free text.
establishing_authorityIdentifierThis field identifies the officer in tactical command that set the range.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
geometryGeometry_circleThis field gives the horizontal geometry of the range: an optional circle around the position of the force at a specified time, for display. When the two do not agree, the range value is correct.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this identification safety range. Other records and orders use it to refer to this identification safety range.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this identification safety range, for display.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about this identification safety range, as free text.
rangeLengthyesThis field gives the identification safety range, as a length with its unit. An aircraft may close to this range from the force without positive identification as a friendly aircraft.
reference_forcestringyesThis field gives the name of the maritime force at the centre of the range.
reference_positionGeoPointThis field gives the geographic position of the maritime force at the time when the range starts, as latitude and longitude. The record gives it only when the position is known.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this identification safety range. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
restrictionslist of stringThis list contains the conditions that control the operations in this identification safety range.
type"ISR"yesThe value identifies this record as an identification safety range. The value selects the data contract of the control measure.

Kill box

urn:openaix:schema:measure-kb:0.2.0-draft.1

measure-kb

A kill box (KB) is a three-dimensional reference system that gives good coordination and control at the correct time, and helps attacks occur quickly. For dynamic targeting operations, it is a permissive fire support coordination measure (FSCM). It decreases the coordination requirements, thus it gives the maximum effects of airpower. Attacks in it occur quickly with less coordination, in the limits of the law of armed conflict (LOAC) and the rules of engagement (ROE). The killbox_kind field gives the type, a blue kill box or a purple kill box, from FM 3-09 (2024), paragraph B-19. The firing status open or closed comes from the assignments in the airspace control order (ACO), not from this record.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
activeActivationyesThis field gives the time interval during which this kill box is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.
channelslist of IdentifierThis list identifies the communications channels of this kill box.
componentslist of AirspaceComponentyesThis list contains the airspace components of the kill box volume. A blue kill box starts at the surface or at its coordinating altitude. A purple kill box has a floor above the surface.
controlling_agencyIdentifierThis field identifies the agency that controls the operations in this kill box.
coordinating_altitudeAltitudeThis field gives the coordinating altitude of the kill box, as an altitude with its unit and reference. A blue kill box can start at this altitude, not at the surface. The source is the multi-service procedures for the kill box (2009).
coordination_instructionslist of stringThis list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this kill box has an effect on.
descriptionstringThis field gives the information about this kill box and its local conditions, as free text.
establishing_authorityIdentifierThis field identifies the authority that set this kill box.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
grid_labelstringThis field gives the grid reference for display, such as a cell and a keypad label, as free text. This field is optional. The components keep the coordinates in WGS 84 decimal degrees.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this kill box. Other records and orders use it to refer to this kill box.
killbox_kindenumyesThis field gives the type of kill box: a blue kill box or a purple kill box, as one of the enumerated values. A blue kill box lets aircraft attack surface targets, and it starts at the surface or at its coordinating altitude. A purple kill box also lets surface units fire at surface targets, and it has an altitude floor.
  • blue Air-to-surface attacks in the kill box occur with no further coordination with the area of operations (AO) commander. The kill box extends from the surface to a ceiling altitude. Units coordinate indirect fires that hit in it or go through it. The coordination is with the airspace control element, the kill box coordinator or the aircrew on station.
  • purple Air-to-surface attacks, surface-to-surface fires and subsurface-to-surface fires in the kill box occur with no further coordination with the area of operations (AO) commander. The kill box has an altitude floor, and aircraft do not fly below the floor. Indirect fires that stay below the floor need no further coordination.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this kill box, for display.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about this kill box, as free text.
purposestringThis field gives the task or objective of this kill box, as free text.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this kill box. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
restrictionslist of stringThis list contains the conditions that control the operations in this kill box.
type"KB"yesThe value identifies this record as a kill box. The value selects the data contract of the control measure.

Coordination line

urn:openaix:schema:measure-line:0.2.0-draft.1

measure-line

A coordination line is a line on the ground, with points in sequence, for the coordination of manoeuvre or identification. The line is the forward line of own troops (FLOT), the forward edge of the battle area (FEBA) or a ground manoeuvre graphic. These graphics are the phase line, the boundary, the limit of advance (LOA), the line of departure (LD) and the line of contact (LC). Other lines show where friendly aircraft set their identification, friend or foe (IFF) equipment to off or on.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
activeActivationyesThis field gives the time interval during which this coordination line is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.
coordination_instructionslist of stringThis list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this coordination line has an effect on.
descriptionstringThis field gives the information about this coordination line and its local conditions, as free text.
establishing_authorityIdentifierThis field identifies the authority that set this coordination line.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
geometryGeometry_line | Geometry_geojson_lineyesThis field gives the horizontal geometry of the line: geographic positions in sequence. A geojson geometry (RFC 7946) of the same shape is also correct.
hostile_sideenumThis field gives the side of the line on which the enemy is, as one of the enumerated values. The side is to the left or to the right of the line when it is followed from its first point to its last point.
  • left The enemy is on the left side of the line, from its first point to its last point.
  • right The enemy is on the right side of the line, from its first point to its last point.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this coordination line. Other records and orders use it to refer to this coordination line.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this coordination line, for display.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about this coordination line, as free text.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this coordination line. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
typeenumyesThis field gives the catalogue code of this control measure, as one of the enumerated values. The code identifies the definition of the control measure in doctrine. The catalogue of control measures gives its class and the source of its definition.
  • FEBA A forward edge of the battle area (FEBA) is the foremost limits of the areas of the ground combat units. It does not include the areas of the covering or screening forces. It helps to coordinate fire support, the positions of forces and manoeuvre.
  • FLOT A forward line of own troops (FLOT) is a line that shows the most forward positions of friendly forces at a given time. This is applicable to any kind of military operation.
  • IFFON An identification, friend or foe switch-on line (IFFON) is a phase line in the airspace control order (ACO). At this line, friendly aircraft start the emission of their identification, friend or foe (IFF) signal. Aircraft start their IFF transponder again at this line, after the mission.
  • IFFOFF An identification, friend or foe switch-off line (IFFOFF) is a phase line in the airspace control order (ACO). At this line, friendly aircraft stop the emission of their identification, friend or foe (IFF) signal. Aircraft stop their IFF transponder at this line, before they go to the target.
  • PL A phase line (PL) is an identifiable feature in the operational area, for the control and coordination of military operations. A phase line is not a boundary, unless the commander designates it as a boundary.
  • BOUNDARY A boundary is a line that delineates surface areas for the coordination and deconfliction of operations. These operations are between units, formations or areas that are next to each other.
  • LOA A limit of advance (LOA) is a phase line that controls the forward progress of the attack. The attack unit does not advance its elements or assets across this line. The unit may move its security forces up to the line.
  • LD A line of departure (LD) is a line in land warfare that coordinates the departure of attack elements.
  • LC A line of contact (LC) is a general trace that delineates the location where friendly and enemy forces engage each other. In the defence, it is frequently the same as the forward line of own troops (FLOT). In an offensive operation, it can be the same as the line of departure (LD).

Missile engagement zone

urn:openaix:schema:measure-mez:0.2.0-draft.1

measure-mez

A missile engagement zone (MEZ) is airspace of defined dimensions in air and missile defence, normally reserved for engagements by surface-to-air missile (SAM) weapon systems. It is an air defence measure. In maritime zone coordination, it is together with the fighter engagement zone (FEZ) and the joint engagement zone (JEZ). Its limits are a sector, an altitude, a range and bearing from a point of origin, or a mixture of these. Aircraft should coordinate before they go into it. The mez_kind field gives the type of zone from JP 3-01 (2012), V-11.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
activeActivationyesThis field gives the time interval during which this missile engagement zone is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.
channelslist of IdentifierThis list identifies the communications channels of this missile engagement zone.
componentslist of AirspaceComponentyesThis list contains the airspace components of the engagement volume. The volume is a sector, or an area with a range and a bearing from the firing unit.
controlling_agencyIdentifierThis field identifies the agency that controls the operations in this missile engagement zone.
coordination_instructionslist of stringThis list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this missile engagement zone has an effect on.
descriptionstringThis field gives the information about this missile engagement zone and its local conditions, as free text.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this missile engagement zone. Other records and orders use it to refer to this missile engagement zone.
mez_kindenumThis field gives the type of missile engagement zone, when the source gives it, as one of the enumerated values. The value is a high-altitude missile engagement zone (HIMEZ), a low- to medium-altitude missile engagement zone (LOMEZ) or a short-range air defence engagement zone (SHORADEZ). Each of the catalogue codes HIMEZ, LOMEZ and SHORADEZ agrees with one of these values.
  • high This value identifies a high-altitude missile engagement zone (HIMEZ), in which high-altitude surface-to-air missiles usually engage the aircraft.
  • low This value identifies a low- to medium-altitude missile engagement zone (LOMEZ), in which surface-to-air missiles for low and moderate altitudes usually engage the aircraft.
  • short_range This value identifies a short-range air defence engagement zone (SHORADEZ), in which short-range air defence (SHORAD) weapons usually engage the aircraft.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this missile engagement zone, for display.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about this missile engagement zone, as free text.
purposestringThis field gives the task or objective of this missile engagement zone, as free text.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this missile engagement zone. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
restrictionslist of stringThis list contains the conditions that control the operations in this missile engagement zone.
type"MEZ"yesThe value identifies this record as a missile engagement zone. The value selects the data contract of the control measure. The code SAMEZ in Table B-5 of North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) also agrees with this value.

Missile arc

urn:openaix:schema:measure-misarc:0.2.0-draft.1

measure-misarc

A missile arc (MISARC) is an area of 10 degrees in maritime operations, or larger when the officer in tactical command gives that order. Its centre is on the bearing of the target, and its range extends to the maximum range of the surface-to-air missile (SAM). The arc has its centre on the firing unit, and its axis is the bearing of the target. Its width is 10 degrees by default, and its range is the maximum range of the surface-to-air missile.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
activeActivationyesThis field gives the time interval during which this missile arc is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.
altitudeAltitudeBlockThis field gives the vertical limits of the arc, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling. This field is optional.
axisBearingyesThis field gives the bearing of the target from the firing unit, as a bearing with its unit and reference. The arc has its centre on this bearing.
centerGeoPointyesThis field gives the geographic position of the firing unit at the centre of the arc, as latitude and longitude.
controlling_agencyIdentifierThis field identifies the agency that controls the operations in this missile arc.
coordination_instructionslist of stringThis list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this missile arc has an effect on.
descriptionstringThis field gives the information about this missile arc and its local conditions, as free text.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
firing_unitstringThis field gives the name of the ship or unit that fires the surface-to-air missile.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this missile arc. Other records and orders use it to refer to this missile arc.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this missile arc, for display.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about this missile arc, as free text.
rangeLengthyesThis field gives the maximum range of the surface-to-air missile, as a length with its unit.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this missile arc. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
restrictionslist of stringThis list contains the conditions that control the operations in this missile arc.
type"MISARC"yesThe value identifies this record as a missile arc. The value selects the data contract of the control measure.
width_degnumberThis field gives the total angular width of the arc, with the axis at its centre, in degrees. The width is 10 degrees, but the officer in tactical command can give an order for a different width.

Air route or corridor

urn:openaix:schema:measure-route:0.2.0-draft.1

measure-route

An air route or corridor is a centreline with points in sequence and with vertical limits. Corridor codes also have a lateral width. Only a published visual flight rules (VFR) route (VFRRTE) can have no vertical limits. The type code gives the task of the route, and it tells if the route has air traffic services. It also gives the area that the route is for: a rear area, a forward area, a maritime force or a base defence zone. Aircraft can fly a corridor in the two directions, but not when its geometry has the one_way flag.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
activeActivationyesThis field gives the time interval during which this route is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.
altitudeAltitudeBlockThis field gives the vertical limits of the route or corridor, as an altitude block with a floor and a ceiling. Each code other than VFRRTE shall have this field. A floor at the surface and a ceiling give a route with a ceiling only.
channelslist of IdentifierThis list identifies the communications channels of this route.
controlling_agencyIdentifierThis field identifies the agency that controls the operations in this route.
coordination_instructionslist of stringThis list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this route has an effect on.
descriptionstringThis field gives the information about this route and its local conditions, as free text.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
geometryGeometry_line | Geometry_corridor | Geometry_path | Geometry_geojson_lineyesThis field gives the horizontal geometry of the route: a centreline, a corridor with its total lateral width, or a path of straight and arc segments. A geojson geometry (RFC 7946) of the same shape is also correct. When doctrine gives a code as a corridor, the code shall use the corridor geometry.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this route. Other records and orders use it to refer to this route.
joinslist of objectThis list contains the other routes that this route joins.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this route, for display.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about this route, as free text.
purposestringThis field gives the task or objective of this route, as free text.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this route. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
restrictionslist of stringThis list contains the conditions that control the operations in this route.
serveslist of objectThis list contains the runways that this route serves. An example is a visual flight rules (VFR) arrival route to a runway.
typeenumyesThis field gives the catalogue code of this control measure, as one of the enumerated values. The code identifies the definition of the control measure in doctrine. The catalogue of control measures gives its class and the source of its definition.
  • AIRRTE An air route (AIRRTE) is the navigable airspace between two points, with only the identification that is necessary to apply flight rules. It is a bi-directional route. It can go through air defences as a minimum-risk route. Only support traffic uses it.
  • LLTR A low-level transit route (LLTR) is a temporary low-level corridor of defined dimensions in the forward area. It decreases the risk to friendly aircraft from friendly air defences or surface forces.
  • SAAFR A slow aviation assets flight route (SAAFR) is a route below the coordination level for land component aviation assets in the forward area. The route is for their movement in direct support of ground operations.
  • SC A special corridor (SC) is an air corridor for the special routing requirements of some missions in air operations.
  • TMRR A temporary minimum-risk route (TMRR) is a temporary minimum-risk route for air traffic. It goes between transit routes, or the rear boundary of the forward area, and its operations area. The route is for direct support of ground operations.
  • TC A transit corridor (TC) is a bi-directional corridor in the rear area that routes aircraft through friendly air defences with minimum risk. Air traffic services are not normally available in it.
  • TR A transit route (TR) is a temporary air corridor of defined dimensions in the forward area for air operations. It decreases the risks to friendly aircraft from friendly air defences or surface forces. It is a bi-directional route, and it should avoid weapons free zones and base defence zones.
  • SL A safe lane (SL) is a bi-directional lane from an airbase, a landing site or a base defence zone (BDZ) to adjacent routes or corridors. It can connect more than one of them. Safe lanes can also connect adjacent activated routes or corridors.
  • APPCOR An approach corridor (APPCOR) is airspace for the safe passage of land-based aircraft that join a maritime force or go from it. The corridor usually goes from an entry and exit gate to the centre of the force. Its inner boundary is the identification safety range (ISR).
  • MRR A minimum-risk route (MRR) is a temporary air corridor of defined dimensions that the ground commander recommends for aircraft. It has the minimum known hazards to low-flying aircraft that transit the combat zone. Aircraft usually use it to cross the forward line of own troops (FLOT). It is usually not near close air support (CAS) target areas.
  • AIRCOR An air corridor (AIRCOR) is a restricted air route of travel for friendly aircraft. Its function is to prevent friendly forces from firing on friendly aircraft. Its altitudes are not more than the coordinating altitude, when there is one.
  • VFRRTE A published visual flight rules route (VFRRTE) is a route on a chart for visual flight rules (VFR) flights around, under or through complex airspace, such as class B airspace. A VFR flyway is a general flight path, not a specific course, and it needs no air traffic control (ATC) clearance. A VFR corridor goes through class B airspace with defined vertical and lateral limits, and it needs no ATC clearance. A VFR transition route is a specific flight course on a chart. On it, communication with ATC is necessary, and an ATC clearance is necessary in class B airspace.
verticeslist of any | anyThis list contains the names and points of the vertices of the route, in order. A vertex that is not in the list has no name.

Traverse level

urn:openaix:schema:measure-tl:0.2.0-draft.1

measure-tl

A traverse level (TL) is the vertical displacement above low-level air defence at which aircraft can cross the area. It is a height and an altitude. It gives the defenders one more procedure to identify friendly aircraft. The record gives the level as a height above the ground and as an altitude above mean sea level.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
activeActivationyesThis field gives the time interval during which this traverse level is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.
coordination_instructionslist of stringThis list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this traverse level has an effect on.
descriptionstringThis field gives the information about this traverse level and its local conditions, as free text.
extensionsExtensionsThis field contains extension data in groups. The namespace of each group identifies the application or standard that supplies its data. The group sim contains the simulator data of the record.
geometryGeometry_vertical & anyyesThis field gives the vertical geometry of the traverse level: a height above the ground and an altitude above mean sea level.
idIdentifieryesThis field identifies this traverse level. Other records and orders use it to refer to this traverse level.
namestringyesThis field gives the name of this traverse level, for display.
notesstringThis field gives the notes about this traverse level, as free text.
resources_refResourceRefThis field identifies the resource catalogue that resolves the references of this traverse level. The reference gives the identifier and the revision of the catalogue.
type"TL"yesThe value identifies this record as a traverse level. The value selects the data contract of the control measure.

Airspace coordination volume

urn:openaix:schema:measure-volume:0.2.0-draft.1

measure-volume

An airspace coordination volume is an airspace with a name and given dimensions, made of components in sequence. Each component has a horizontal boundary, a floor and a ceiling. The type is a code from North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) AJP-3.3.5 Annex B or from doctrine. The code gives the task of the volume and the airspace users that can or cannot go in it. The agency that controls the volume does the coordination of entry and operations.

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
$schemastringThis field identifies the schema that validates this document.
activeActivationyesThis field gives the time interval during which this airspace coordination volume is active. The value is an interval with a start and an end, a schedule for each week, or continuous activation.
channelslist of IdentifierThis list identifies the communications channels of this airspace coordination volume.
componentslist of AirspaceComponentyesThis list contains the airspace components of the volume, in order. Each component has a horizontal boundary, a floor and a ceiling.
controlling_agencyIdentifierThis field identifies the agency that controls the operations in this airspace coordination volume.
coordination_instructionslist of stringThis list contains the instructions that coordinate entry, operations and handover. The instructions are for the agencies or forces that this airspace coordination volume has an effect on.
descriptionstringThis field gives the information about this airspace coordination volume and its local conditions, as free text.
